# Job {.unnumbered}

##### Chapter 1

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="1">
<p><span class="drop-cap">T</span>here was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared God, and eschewed evil. <span class="verse-number">2</span> And there were born unto him seven sons and three daughters. <span class="verse-number">3</span> His substance also was seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she asses, and a very great household; so that this man was the greatest of all the men of the east. <span class="verse-number">4</span> And his sons went and feasted in their houses, every one his day; and sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them. <span class="verse-number">5</span> And it was so, when the days of their feasting were gone about, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all: for Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually. <span class="verse-number">6</span> Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan came also among them. <span class="verse-number">7</span> And the LORD said unto Satan, Whence comest thou? Then Satan answered the LORD, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it. <span class="verse-number">8</span> And the LORD said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil? <span class="verse-number">9</span> Then Satan answered the LORD, and said, Doth Job fear God for nought? <span class="verse-number">10</span> Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side? thou hast blessed the work of his hands, and his substance is increased in the land. <span class="verse-number">11</span> But put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face. <span class="verse-number">12</span> And the LORD said unto Satan, Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand. So Satan went forth from the presence of the LORD. <span class="verse-number">13</span> And there was a day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house: <span class="verse-number">14</span> And there came a messenger unto Job, and said, The oxen were plowing, and the asses feeding beside them: <span class="verse-number">15</span> And the Sabeans fell upon them, and took them away; yea, they have slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee. <span class="verse-number">16</span> While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The fire of God is fallen from heaven, and hath burned up the sheep, and the servants, and consumed them; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee. <span class="verse-number">17</span> While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The Chaldeans made out three bands, and fell upon the camels, and have carried them away, yea, and slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee. <span class="verse-number">18</span> While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, Thy sons and thy daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house: <span class="verse-number">19</span> And, behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and smote the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young men, and they are dead; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee. <span class="verse-number">20</span> Then Job arose, and rent his mantle, and shaved his head, and fell down upon the ground, and worshipped, <span class="verse-number">21</span> And said, Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither: the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD. <span class="verse-number">22</span> In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly.</p>
</div>
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
\begin{scripture}[Job][1]
\lettrine[lines=4]{T}{here} was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared God, and eschewed evil.
\vs{2}And there were born unto him seven sons and three daughters.
\vs{3}His substance also was seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she asses, and a very great household; so that this man was the greatest of all the men of the east.
\vs{4}And his sons went and feasted in their houses, every one his day; and sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.
\vs{5}And it was so, when the days of their feasting were gone about, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all: for Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually.
\vs{6}Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan came also among them.
\vs{7}And the LORD said unto Satan, Whence comest thou? Then Satan answered the LORD, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.
\vs{8}And the LORD said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil?
\vs{9}Then Satan answered the LORD, and said, Doth Job fear God for nought?
\vs{10}Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side? thou hast blessed the work of his hands, and his substance is increased in the land.
\vs{11}But put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.
\vs{12}And the LORD said unto Satan, Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand. So Satan went forth from the presence of the LORD.
\vs{13}And there was a day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house:
\vs{14}And there came a messenger unto Job, and said, The oxen were plowing, and the asses feeding beside them:
\vs{15}And the Sabeans fell upon them, and took them away; yea, they have slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.
\vs{16}While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The fire of God is fallen from heaven, and hath burned up the sheep, and the servants, and consumed them; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.
\vs{17}While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The Chaldeans made out three bands, and fell upon the camels, and have carried them away, yea, and slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.
\vs{18}While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, Thy sons and thy daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house:
\vs{19}And, behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and smote the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young men, and they are dead; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.
\vs{20}Then Job arose, and rent his mantle, and shaved his head, and fell down upon the ground, and worshipped,
\vs{21}And said, Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither: the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.
\vs{22}In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly.
\end{scripture}
:::


##### Chapter 2

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="2">
<p><span class="drop-cap">A</span>gain there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan came also among them to present himself before the LORD. <span class="verse-number">2</span> And the LORD said unto Satan, From whence comest thou? And Satan answered the LORD, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it. <span class="verse-number">3</span> And the LORD said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil? and still he holdeth fast his integrity, although thou movedst me against him, to destroy him without cause. <span class="verse-number">4</span> And Satan answered the LORD, and said, Skin for skin, yea, all that a man hath will he give for his life. <span class="verse-number">5</span> But put forth thine hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will curse thee to thy face. <span class="verse-number">6</span> And the LORD said unto Satan, Behold, he is in thine hand; but save his life. <span class="verse-number">7</span> So went Satan forth from the presence of the LORD, and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown. <span class="verse-number">8</span> And he took him a potsherd to scrape himself withal; and he sat down among the ashes. <span class="verse-number">9</span> Then said his wife unto him, Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die. <span class="verse-number">10</span> But he said unto her, Thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh. What? shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil? In all this did not Job sin with his lips. <span class="verse-number">11</span> Now when Job's three friends heard of all this evil that was come upon him, they came every one from his own place; Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite: for they had made an appointment together to come to mourn with him and to comfort him. <span class="verse-number">12</span> And when they lifted up their eyes afar off, and knew him not, they lifted up their voice, and wept; and they rent every one his mantle, and sprinkled dust upon their heads toward heaven. <span class="verse-number">13</span> So they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great.</p>
</div>
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
\begin{scripture}[Job][2]
\lettrine[lines=4]{A}{gain} there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan came also among them to present himself before the LORD.
\vs{2}And the LORD said unto Satan, From whence comest thou? And Satan answered the LORD, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.
\vs{3}And the LORD said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil? and still he holdeth fast his integrity, although thou movedst me against him, to destroy him without cause.
\vs{4}And Satan answered the LORD, and said, Skin for skin, yea, all that a man hath will he give for his life.
\vs{5}But put forth thine hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will curse thee to thy face.
\vs{6}And the LORD said unto Satan, Behold, he is in thine hand; but save his life.
\vs{7}So went Satan forth from the presence of the LORD, and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown.
\vs{8}And he took him a potsherd to scrape himself withal; and he sat down among the ashes.
\vs{9}Then said his wife unto him, Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die.
\vs{10}But he said unto her, Thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh. What? shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil? In all this did not Job sin with his lips.
\vs{11}Now when Job's three friends heard of all this evil that was come upon him, they came every one from his own place; Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite: for they had made an appointment together to come to mourn with him and to comfort him.
\vs{12}And when they lifted up their eyes afar off, and knew him not, they lifted up their voice, and wept; and they rent every one his mantle, and sprinkled dust upon their heads toward heaven.
\vs{13}So they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great.
\end{scripture}

##### Chapter 3

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="3">
<p><span class="drop-cap">A</span>fter this opened Job his mouth, and cursed his day. <span class="verse-number">2</span> And Job spake, and said, <span class="verse-number">3</span> Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said, There is a man child conceived. <span class="verse-number">4</span> Let that day be darkness; let not God regard it from above, neither let the light shine upon it. <span class="verse-number">5</span> Let darkness and the shadow of death stain it; let a cloud dwell upon it; let the blackness of the day terrify it. <span class="verse-number">6</span> As for that night, let darkness seize upon it; let it not be joined unto the days of the year, let it not come into the number of the months. <span class="verse-number">7</span> Lo, let that night be solitary, let no joyful voice come therein. <span class="verse-number">8</span> Let them curse it that curse the day, who are ready to raise up their mourning. <span class="verse-number">9</span> Let the stars of the twilight thereof be dark; let it look for light, but have none; neither let it see the dawning of the day: <span class="verse-number">10</span> Because it shut not up the doors of my mother's womb, nor hid sorrow from mine eyes. <span class="verse-number">11</span> Why died I not from the womb? why did I not give up the ghost when I came out of the belly? <span class="verse-number">12</span> Why did the knees prevent me? or why the breasts that I should suck? <span class="verse-number">13</span> For now should I have lain still and been quiet, I should have slept: then had I been at rest, <span class="verse-number">14</span> With kings and counsellors of the earth, which build desolate places for themselves; <span class="verse-number">15</span> Or with princes that had gold, who filled their houses with silver: <span class="verse-number">16</span> Or as an hidden untimely birth I had not been; as infants which never saw light. <span class="verse-number">17</span> There the wicked cease from troubling; and there the weary be at rest. <span class="verse-number">18</span> There the prisoners rest together; they hear not the voice of the oppressor. <span class="verse-number">19</span> The small and great are there; and the servant is free from his master. <span class="verse-number">20</span> Wherefore is light given to him that is in misery, and life unto the bitter in soul; <span class="verse-number">21</span> Which long for death, but it cometh not; and dig for it more than for hid treasures; <span class="verse-number">22</span> Which rejoice exceedingly, and are glad, when they can find the grave? <span class="verse-number">23</span> Why is light given to a man whose way is hid, and whom God hath hedged in? <span class="verse-number">24</span> For my sighing cometh before I eat, and my roarings are poured out like the waters. <span class="verse-number">25</span> For the thing which I greatly feared is come upon me, and that which I was afraid of is come unto me. <span class="verse-number">26</span> I was not in safety, neither had I rest, neither was I quiet; yet trouble came.</p>
</div>
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
\begin{scripture}[Job][3]
\lettrine[lines=4]{A}{fter} this opened Job his mouth, and cursed his day.
\vs{2}And Job spake, and said,
\vs{3}Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said, There is a man child conceived.
\vs{4}Let that day be darkness; let not God regard it from above, neither let the light shine upon it.
\vs{5}Let darkness and the shadow of death stain it; let a cloud dwell upon it; let the blackness of the day terrify it.
\vs{6}As for that night, let darkness seize upon it; let it not be joined unto the days of the year, let it not come into the number of the months.
\vs{7}Lo, let that night be solitary, let no joyful voice come therein.
\vs{8}Let them curse it that curse the day, who are ready to raise up their mourning.
\vs{9}Let the stars of the twilight thereof be dark; let it look for light, but have none; neither let it see the dawning of the day:
\vs{10}Because it shut not up the doors of my mother's womb, nor hid sorrow from mine eyes.
\vs{11}Why died I not from the womb? why did I not give up the ghost when I came out of the belly?
\vs{12}Why did the knees prevent me? or why the breasts that I should suck?
\vs{13}For now should I have lain still and been quiet, I should have slept: then had I been at rest,
\vs{14}With kings and counsellors of the earth, which build desolate places for themselves;
\vs{15}Or with princes that had gold, who filled their houses with silver:
\vs{16}Or as an hidden untimely birth I had not been; as infants which never saw light.
\vs{17}There the wicked cease from troubling; and there the weary be at rest.
\vs{18}There the prisoners rest together; they hear not the voice of the oppressor.
\vs{19}The small and great are there; and the servant is free from his master.
\vs{20}Wherefore is light given to him that is in misery, and life unto the bitter in soul;
\vs{21}Which long for death, but it cometh not; and dig for it more than for hid treasures;
\vs{22}Which rejoice exceedingly, and are glad, when they can find the grave?
\vs{23}Why is light given to a man whose way is hid, and whom God hath hedged in?
\vs{24}For my sighing cometh before I eat, and my roarings are poured out like the waters.
\vs{25}For the thing which I greatly feared is come upon me, and that which I was afraid of is come unto me.
\vs{26}I was not in safety, neither had I rest, neither was I quiet; yet trouble came.
\end{scripture}
:::


##### Chapter 4

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="4">
<p><span class="drop-cap">T</span>hen Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said, <span class="verse-number">2</span> If we assay to commune with thee, wilt thou be grieved? but who can withhold himself from speaking? <span class="verse-number">3</span> Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands. <span class="verse-number">4</span> Thy words have upholden him that was falling, and thou hast strengthened the feeble knees. <span class="verse-number">5</span> But now it is come upon thee, and thou faintest; it toucheth thee, and thou art troubled. <span class="verse-number">6</span> Is not this thy fear, thy confidence, thy hope, and the uprightness of thy ways? <span class="verse-number">7</span> Remember, I pray thee, who ever perished, being innocent? or where were the righteous cut off? <span class="verse-number">8</span> Even as I have seen, they that plow iniquity, and sow wickedness, reap the same. <span class="verse-number">9</span> By the blast of God they perish, and by the breath of his nostrils are they consumed. <span class="verse-number">10</span> The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, and the teeth of the young lions, are broken. <span class="verse-number">11</span> The old lion perisheth for lack of prey, and the stout lion's whelps are scattered abroad. <span class="verse-number">12</span> Now a thing was secretly brought to me, and mine ear received a little thereof. <span class="verse-number">13</span> In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falleth on men, <span class="verse-number">14</span> Fear came upon me, and trembling, which made all my bones to shake. <span class="verse-number">15</span> Then a spirit passed before my face; the hair of my flesh stood up: <span class="verse-number">16</span> It stood still, but I could not discern the form thereof: an image was before mine eyes, there was silence, and I heard a voice, saying, <span class="verse-number">17</span> Shall mortal man be more just than God? shall a man be more pure than his maker? <span class="verse-number">18</span> Behold, he put no trust in his servants; and his angels he charged with folly: <span class="verse-number">19</span> How much less in them that dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, which are crushed before the moth? <span class="verse-number">20</span> They are destroyed from morning to evening: they perish for ever without any regarding it. <span class="verse-number">21</span> Doth not their excellency which is in them go away? they die, even without wisdom.</p>
</div>
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
\begin{scripture}[Job][4]
\lettrine[lines=4]{T}{hen} Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said,
\vs{2}If we assay to commune with thee, wilt thou be grieved? but who can withhold himself from speaking?
\vs{3}Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands.
\vs{4}Thy words have upholden him that was falling, and thou hast strengthened the feeble knees.
\vs{5}But now it is come upon thee, and thou faintest; it toucheth thee, and thou art troubled.
\vs{6}Is not this thy fear, thy confidence, thy hope, and the uprightness of thy ways?
\vs{7}Remember, I pray thee, who ever perished, being innocent? or where were the righteous cut off?
\vs{8}Even as I have seen, they that plow iniquity, and sow wickedness, reap the same.
\vs{9}By the blast of God they perish, and by the breath of his nostrils are they consumed.
\vs{10}The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, and the teeth of the young lions, are broken.
\vs{11}The old lion perisheth for lack of prey, and the stout lion's whelps are scattered abroad.
\vs{12}Now a thing was secretly brought to me, and mine ear received a little thereof.
\vs{13}In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falleth on men,
\vs{14}Fear came upon me, and trembling, which made all my bones to shake.
\vs{15}Then a spirit passed before my face; the hair of my flesh stood up:
\vs{16}It stood still, but I could not discern the form thereof: an image was before mine eyes, there was silence, and I heard a voice, saying,
\vs{17}Shall mortal man be more just than God? shall a man be more pure than his maker?
\vs{18}Behold, he put no trust in his servants; and his angels he charged with folly:
\vs{19}How much less in them that dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, which are crushed before the moth?
\vs{20}They are destroyed from morning to evening: they perish for ever without any regarding it.
\vs{21}Doth not their excellency which is in them go away? they die, even without wisdom.
\end{scripture}
:::


##### Chapter 5

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="5">
<p><span class="drop-cap">C</span>all now, if there be any that will answer thee; and to which of the saints wilt thou turn? <span class="verse-number">2</span> For wrath killeth the foolish man, and envy slayeth the silly one. <span class="verse-number">3</span> I have seen the foolish taking root: but suddenly I cursed his habitation. <span class="verse-number">4</span> His children are far from safety, and they are crushed in the gate, neither is there any to deliver them. <span class="verse-number">5</span> Whose harvest the hungry eateth up, and taketh it even out of the thorns, and the robber swalloweth up their substance. <span class="verse-number">6</span> Although affliction cometh not forth of the dust, neither doth trouble spring out of the ground; <span class="verse-number">7</span> Yet man is born unto trouble, as the sparks fly upward. <span class="verse-number">8</span> I would seek unto God, and unto God would I commit my cause: <span class="verse-number">9</span> Which doeth great things and unsearchable; marvellous things without number: <span class="verse-number">10</span> Who giveth rain upon the earth, and sendeth waters upon the fields: <span class="verse-number">11</span> To set up on high those that be low; that those which mourn may be exalted to safety. <span class="verse-number">12</span> He disappointeth the devices of the crafty, so that their hands cannot perform their enterprise. <span class="verse-number">13</span> He taketh the wise in their own craftiness: and the counsel of the froward is carried headlong. <span class="verse-number">14</span> They meet with darkness in the day time, and grope in the noonday as in the night. <span class="verse-number">15</span> But he saveth the poor from the sword, from their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty. <span class="verse-number">16</span> So the poor hath hope, and iniquity stoppeth her mouth. <span class="verse-number">17</span> Behold, happy is the man whom God correcteth: therefore despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty: <span class="verse-number">18</span> For he maketh sore, and bindeth up: he woundeth, and his hands make whole. <span class="verse-number">19</span> He shall deliver thee in six troubles: yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee. <span class="verse-number">20</span> In famine he shall redeem thee from death: and in war from the power of the sword. <span class="verse-number">21</span> Thou shalt be hid from the scourge of the tongue: neither shalt thou be afraid of destruction when it cometh. <span class="verse-number">22</span> At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh: neither shalt thou be afraid of the beasts of the earth. <span class="verse-number">23</span> For thou shalt be in league with the stones of the field: and the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee. <span class="verse-number">24</span> And thou shalt know that thy tabernacle shall be in peace; and thou shalt visit thy habitation, and shalt not sin. <span class="verse-number">25</span> Thou shalt know also that thy seed shall be great, and thine offspring as the grass of the earth. <span class="verse-number">26</span> Thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age, like as a shock of corn cometh in in his season. <span class="verse-number">27</span> Lo this, we have searched it, so it is; hear it, and know thou it for thy good.</p>
</div>
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
\begin{scripture}[Job][5]
\lettrine[lines=4]{C}{all} now, if there be any that will answer thee; and to which of the saints wilt thou turn?
\vs{2}For wrath killeth the foolish man, and envy slayeth the silly one.
\vs{3}I have seen the foolish taking root: but suddenly I cursed his habitation.
\vs{4}His children are far from safety, and they are crushed in the gate, neither is there any to deliver them.
\vs{5}Whose harvest the hungry eateth up, and taketh it even out of the thorns, and the robber swalloweth up their substance.
\vs{6}Although affliction cometh not forth of the dust, neither doth trouble spring out of the ground;
\vs{7}Yet man is born unto trouble, as the sparks fly upward.
\vs{8}I would seek unto God, and unto God would I commit my cause:
\vs{9}Which doeth great things and unsearchable; marvellous things without number:
\vs{10}Who giveth rain upon the earth, and sendeth waters upon the fields:
\vs{11}To set up on high those that be low; that those which mourn may be exalted to safety.
\vs{12}He disappointeth the devices of the crafty, so that their hands cannot perform their enterprise.
\vs{13}He taketh the wise in their own craftiness: and the counsel of the froward is carried headlong.
\vs{14}They meet with darkness in the day time, and grope in the noonday as in the night.
\vs{15}But he saveth the poor from the sword, from their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty.
\vs{16}So the poor hath hope, and iniquity stoppeth her mouth.
\vs{17}Behold, happy is the man whom God correcteth: therefore despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty:
\vs{18}For he maketh sore, and bindeth up: he woundeth, and his hands make whole.
\vs{19}He shall deliver thee in six troubles: yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee.
\vs{20}In famine he shall redeem thee from death: and in war from the power of the sword.
\vs{21}Thou shalt be hid from the scourge of the tongue: neither shalt thou be afraid of destruction when it cometh.
\vs{22}At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh: neither shalt thou be afraid of the beasts of the earth.
\vs{23}For thou shalt be in league with the stones of the field: and the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee.
\vs{24}And thou shalt know that thy tabernacle shall be in peace; and thou shalt visit thy habitation, and shalt not sin.
\vs{25}Thou shalt know also that thy seed shall be great, and thine offspring as the grass of the earth.
\vs{26}Thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age, like as a shock of corn cometh in in his season.
\vs{27}Lo this, we have searched it, so it is; hear it, and know thou it for thy good.
\end{scripture}
:::


##### Chapter 6

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="6">
<p><span class="drop-cap">B</span>ut Job answered and said, <span class="verse-number">2</span> Oh that my grief were throughly weighed, and my calamity laid in the balances together! <span class="verse-number">3</span> For now it would be heavier than the sand of the sea: therefore my words are swallowed up. <span class="verse-number">4</span> For the arrows of the Almighty are within me, the poison whereof drinketh up my spirit: the terrors of God do set themselves in array against me. <span class="verse-number">5</span> Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? or loweth the ox over his fodder? <span class="verse-number">6</span> Can that which is unsavoury be eaten without salt? or is there any taste in the white of an egg? <span class="verse-number">7</span> The things that my soul refused to touch are as my sorrowful meat. <span class="verse-number">8</span> Oh that I might have my request; and that God would grant me the thing that I long for! <span class="verse-number">9</span> Even that it would please God to destroy me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off! <span class="verse-number">10</span> Then should I yet have comfort; yea, I would harden myself in sorrow: let him not spare; for I have not concealed the words of the Holy One. <span class="verse-number">11</span> What is my strength, that I should hope? and what is mine end, that I should prolong my life? <span class="verse-number">12</span> Is my strength the strength of stones? or is my flesh of brass? <span class="verse-number">13</span> Is not my help in me? and is wisdom driven quite from me? <span class="verse-number">14</span> To him that is afflicted pity should be shewed from his friend; but he forsaketh the fear of the Almighty. <span class="verse-number">15</span> My brethren have dealt deceitfully as a brook, and as the stream of brooks they pass away; <span class="verse-number">16</span> Which are blackish by reason of the ice, and wherein the snow is hid: <span class="verse-number">17</span> What time they wax warm, they vanish: when it is hot, they are consumed out of their place. <span class="verse-number">18</span> The paths of their way are turned aside; they go to nothing, and perish. <span class="verse-number">19</span> The troops of Tema looked, the companies of Sheba waited for them. <span class="verse-number">20</span> They were confounded because they had hoped; they came thither, and were ashamed. <span class="verse-number">21</span> For now ye are nothing; ye see my casting down, and are afraid. <span class="verse-number">22</span> Did I say, Bring unto me? or, Give a reward for me of your substance? <span class="verse-number">23</span> Or, Deliver me from the enemy's hand? or, Redeem me from the hand of the mighty? <span class="verse-number">24</span> Teach me, and I will hold my tongue: and cause me to understand wherein I have erred. <span class="verse-number">25</span> How forcible are right words! but what doth your arguing reprove? <span class="verse-number">26</span> Do ye imagine to reprove words, and the speeches of one that is desperate, which are as wind? <span class="verse-number">27</span> Yea, ye overwhelm the fatherless, and ye dig a pit for your friend. <span class="verse-number">28</span> Now therefore be content, look upon me; for it is evident unto you if I lie. <span class="verse-number">29</span> Return, I pray you, let it not be iniquity; yea, return again, my righteousness is in it. <span class="verse-number">30</span> Is there iniquity in my tongue? cannot my taste discern perverse things?</p>
</div>
:::

##### Chapter 7

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="7">
<p><span class="drop-cap">I</span>s there not an appointed time to man upon earth? are not his days also like the days of an hireling? <span class="verse-number">2</span> As a servant earnestly desireth the shadow, and as an hireling looketh for the reward of his work: <span class="verse-number">3</span> So am I made to possess months of vanity, and wearisome nights are appointed to me. <span class="verse-number">4</span> When I lie down, I say, When shall I arise, and the night be gone? and I am full of tossings to and fro unto the dawning of the day. <span class="verse-number">5</span> My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; my skin is broken, and become loathsome. <span class="verse-number">6</span> My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, and are spent without hope. <span class="verse-number">7</span> O remember that my life is wind: mine eye shall no more see good. <span class="verse-number">8</span> The eye of him that hath seen me shall see me no more: thine eyes are upon me, and I am not. <span class="verse-number">9</span> As the cloud is consumed and vanisheth away: so he that goeth down to the grave shall come up no more. <span class="verse-number">10</span> He shall return no more to his house, neither shall his place know him any more. <span class="verse-number">11</span> Therefore I will not refrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul. <span class="verse-number">12</span> Am I a sea, or a whale, that thou settest a watch over me? <span class="verse-number">13</span> When I say, My bed shall comfort me, my couch shall ease my complaints; <span class="verse-number">14</span> Then thou scarest me with dreams, and terrifiest me through visions: <span class="verse-number">15</span> So that my soul chooseth strangling, and death rather than my life. <span class="verse-number">16</span> I loathe it; I would not live alway: let me alone; for my days are vanity. <span class="verse-number">17</span> What is man, that thou shouldest magnify him? and that thou shouldest set thine heart upon him? <span class="verse-number">18</span> And that thou shouldest visit him every morning, and try him every moment? <span class="verse-number">19</span> How long wilt thou not depart from me, nor let me alone till I swallow down my spittle? <span class="verse-number">20</span> I have sinned; what shall I do unto thee, O thou preserver of men? why hast thou set me as a mark against thee, so that I am a burden to myself? <span class="verse-number">21</span> And why dost thou not pardon my transgression, and take away my iniquity? for now shall I sleep in the dust; and thou shalt seek me in the morning, but I shall not be.</p>
</div>
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}

\vs{4}When I lie down, I say, When shall I arise, and the night be gone? and I am full of tossings to and fro unto the dawning of the day.
\vs{5}My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; my skin is broken, and become loathsome.
\vs{6}My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, and are spent without hope.
\vs{7}O remember that my life is wind: mine eye shall no more see good.
\vs{8}The eye of him that hath seen me shall see me no more: thine eyes are upon me, and I am not.
\vs{9}As the cloud is consumed and vanisheth away: so he that goeth down to the grave shall come up no more.
\vs{10}He shall return no more to his house, neither shall his place know him any more.
\vs{11}Therefore I will not refrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
\vs{12}Am I a sea, or a whale, that thou settest a watch over me?

##### Chapter 8

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="8">
<p><span class="drop-cap">T</span>hen answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said, <span class="verse-number">2</span> How long wilt thou speak these things? and how long shall the words of thy mouth be like a strong wind? <span class="verse-number">3</span> Doth God pervert judgment? or doth the Almighty pervert justice? <span class="verse-number">4</span> If thy children have sinned against him, and he have cast them away for their transgression; <span class="verse-number">5</span> If thou wouldest seek unto God betimes, and make thy supplication to the Almighty; <span class="verse-number">6</span> If thou wert pure and upright; surely now he would awake for thee, and make the habitation of thy righteousness prosperous. <span class="verse-number">7</span> Though thy beginning was small, yet thy latter end should greatly increase. <span class="verse-number">8</span> For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers: <span class="verse-number">9</span> (For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days upon earth are a shadow:) <span class="verse-number">10</span> Shall not they teach thee, and tell thee, and utter words out of their heart? <span class="verse-number">11</span> Can the rush grow up without mire? can the flag grow without water? <span class="verse-number">12</span> Whilst it is yet in his greenness, and not cut down, it withereth before any other herb. <span class="verse-number">13</span> So are the paths of all that forget God; and the hypocrite's hope shall perish: <span class="verse-number">14</span> Whose hope shall be cut off, and whose trust shall be a spider's web. <span class="verse-number">15</span> He shall lean upon his house, but it shall not stand: he shall hold it fast, but it shall not endure. <span class="verse-number">16</span> He is green before the sun, and his branch shooteth forth in his garden. <span class="verse-number">17</span> His roots are wrapped about the heap, and seeth the place of stones. <span class="verse-number">18</span> If he destroy him from his place, then it shall deny him, saying, I have not seen thee. <span class="verse-number">19</span> Behold, this is the joy of his way, and out of the earth shall others grow. <span class="verse-number">20</span> Behold, God will not cast away a perfect man, neither will he help the evil doers: <span class="verse-number">21</span> Till he fill thy mouth with laughing, and thy lips with rejoicing. <span class="verse-number">22</span> They that hate thee shall be clothed with shame; and the dwelling place of the wicked shall come to nought.</p>
</div>
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
\begin{scripture}[Job][8]
\lettrine[lines=4]{T}{hen} answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,
\vs{2}How long wilt thou speak these things? and how long shall the words of thy mouth be like a strong wind?
\vs{3}Doth God pervert judgment? or doth the Almighty pervert justice?
\vs{4}If thy children have sinned against him, and he have cast them away for their transgression;
\vs{5}If thou wouldest seek unto God betimes, and make thy supplication to the Almighty;
\vs{6}If thou wert pure and upright; surely now he would awake for thee, and make the habitation of thy righteousness prosperous.
\vs{7}Though thy beginning was small, yet thy latter end should greatly increase.
\vs{8}For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers:
\vs{9}(For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days upon earth are a shadow:)
\vs{10}Shall not they teach thee, and tell thee, and utter words out of their heart?
\vs{11}Can the rush grow up without mire? can the flag grow without water?
\vs{12}Whilst it is yet in his greenness, and not cut down, it withereth before any other herb.
\vs{13}So are the paths of all that forget God; and the hypocrite's hope shall perish:
\vs{14}Whose hope shall be cut off, and whose trust shall be a spider's web.
\vs{15}He shall lean upon his house, but it shall not stand: he shall hold it fast, but it shall not endure.
\vs{16}He is green before the sun, and his branch shooteth forth in his garden.
\vs{17}His roots are wrapped about the heap, and seeth the place of stones.
\vs{18}If he destroy him from his place, then it shall deny him, saying, I have not seen thee.
\vs{19}Behold, this is the joy of his way, and out of the earth shall others grow.
\vs{20}Behold, God will not cast away a perfect man, neither will he help the evil doers:
\vs{21}Till he fill thy mouth with laughing, and thy lips with rejoicing.
\vs{22}They that hate thee shall be clothed with shame; and the dwelling place of the wicked shall come to nought.
\end{scripture}

##### Chapter 9

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="9">
<p><span class="drop-cap">T</span>hen Job answered and said, <span class="verse-number">2</span> I know it is so of a truth: but how should man be just with God? <span class="verse-number">3</span> If he will contend with him, he cannot answer him one of a thousand. <span class="verse-number">4</span> He is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who hath hardened himself against him, and hath prospered? <span class="verse-number">5</span> Which removeth the mountains, and they know not: which overturneth them in his anger. <span class="verse-number">6</span> Which shaketh the earth out of her place, and the pillars thereof tremble. <span class="verse-number">7</span> Which commandeth the sun, and it riseth not; and sealeth up the stars. <span class="verse-number">8</span> Which alone spreadeth out the heavens, and treadeth upon the waves of the sea. <span class="verse-number">9</span> Which maketh Arcturus, Orion, and Pleiades, and the chambers of the south. <span class="verse-number">10</span> Which doeth great things past finding out; yea, and wonders without number. <span class="verse-number">11</span> Lo, he goeth by me, and I see him not: he passeth on also, but I perceive him not. <span class="verse-number">12</span> Behold, he taketh away, who can hinder him? who will say unto him, What doest thou? <span class="verse-number">13</span> If God will not withdraw his anger, the proud helpers do stoop under him. <span class="verse-number">14</span> How much less shall I answer him, and choose out my words to reason with him? <span class="verse-number">15</span> Whom, though I were righteous, yet would I not answer, but I would make supplication to my judge. <span class="verse-number">16</span> If I had called, and he had answered me; yet would I not believe that he had hearkened unto my voice. <span class="verse-number">17</span> For he breaketh me with a tempest, and multiplieth my wounds without cause. <span class="verse-number">18</span> He will not suffer me to take my breath, but filleth me with bitterness. <span class="verse-number">19</span> If I speak of strength, lo, he is strong: and if of judgment, who shall set me a time to plead? <span class="verse-number">20</span> If I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me: if I say, I am perfect, it shall also prove me perverse. <span class="verse-number">21</span> Though I were perfect, yet would I not know my soul: I would despise my life. <span class="verse-number">22</span> This is one thing, therefore I said it, He destroyeth the perfect and the wicked. <span class="verse-number">23</span> If the scourge slay suddenly, he will laugh at the trial of the innocent. <span class="verse-number">24</span> The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof; if not, where, and who is he? <span class="verse-number">25</span> Now my days are swifter than a post: they flee away, they see no good. <span class="verse-number">26</span> They are passed away as the swift ships: as the eagle that hasteth to the prey. <span class="verse-number">27</span> If I say, I will forget my complaint, I will leave off my heaviness, and comfort myself: <span class="verse-number">28</span> I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that thou wilt not hold me innocent. <span class="verse-number">29</span> If I be wicked, why then labour I in vain? <span class="verse-number">30</span> If I wash myself with snow water, and make my hands never so clean; <span class="verse-number">31</span> Yet shalt thou plunge me in the ditch, and mine own clothes shall abhor me. <span class="verse-number">32</span> For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, and we should come together in judgment. <span class="verse-number">33</span> Neither is there any daysman betwixt us, that might lay his hand upon us both. <span class="verse-number">34</span> Let him take his rod away from me, and let not his fear terrify me: <span class="verse-number">35</span> Then would I speak, and not fear him; but it is not so with me.</p>
</div>
:::

##### Chapter 10

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="10">
<p><span class="drop-cap">M</span>y soul is weary of my life; I will leave my complaint upon myself; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul. <span class="verse-number">2</span> I will say unto God, Do not condemn me; shew me wherefore thou contendest with me. <span class="verse-number">3</span> Is it good unto thee that thou shouldest oppress, that thou shouldest despise the work of thine hands, and shine upon the counsel of the wicked? <span class="verse-number">4</span> Hast thou eyes of flesh? or seest thou as man seeth? <span class="verse-number">5</span> Are thy days as the days of man? are thy years as man's days, <span class="verse-number">6</span> That thou enquirest after mine iniquity, and searchest after my sin? <span class="verse-number">7</span> Thou knowest that I am not wicked; and there is none that can deliver out of thine hand. <span class="verse-number">8</span> Thine hands have made me and fashioned me together round about; yet thou dost destroy me. <span class="verse-number">9</span> Remember, I beseech thee, that thou hast made me as the clay; and wilt thou bring me into dust again? <span class="verse-number">10</span> Hast thou not poured me out as milk, and curdled me like cheese? <span class="verse-number">11</span> Thou hast clothed me with skin and flesh, and hast fenced me with bones and sinews. <span class="verse-number">12</span> Thou hast granted me life and favour, and thy visitation hath preserved my spirit. <span class="verse-number">13</span> And these things hast thou hid in thine heart: I know that this is with thee. <span class="verse-number">14</span> If I sin, then thou markest me, and thou wilt not acquit me from mine iniquity. <span class="verse-number">15</span> If I be wicked, woe unto me; and if I be righteous, yet will I not lift up my head. I am full of confusion; therefore see thou mine affliction; <span class="verse-number">16</span> For it increaseth. Thou huntest me as a fierce lion: and again thou shewest thyself marvellous upon me. <span class="verse-number">17</span> Thou renewest thy witnesses against me, and increasest thine indignation upon me; changes and war are against me. <span class="verse-number">18</span> Wherefore then hast thou brought me forth out of the womb? Oh that I had given up the ghost, and no eye had seen me! <span class="verse-number">19</span> I should have been as though I had not been; I should have been carried from the womb to the grave. <span class="verse-number">20</span> Are not my days few? cease then, and let me alone, that I may take comfort a little, <span class="verse-number">21</span> Before I go whence I shall not return, even to the land of darkness and the shadow of death; <span class="verse-number">22</span> A land of darkness, as darkness itself; and of the shadow of death, without any order, and where the light is as darkness.</p>
</div>
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}

\lettrine[lines=4]{M}{y} soul is weary of my life; I will leave my complaint upon myself; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
\vs{2}I will say unto God, Do not condemn me; shew me wherefore thou contendest with me.

\vs{4}Hast thou eyes of flesh? or seest thou as man seeth?
\vs{5}Are thy days as the days of man? are thy years as man's days,
\vs{6}That thou enquirest after mine iniquity, and searchest after my sin?
\vs{7}Thou knowest that I am not wicked; and there is none that can deliver out of thine hand.
\vs{8}Thine hands have made me and fashioned me together round about; yet thou dost destroy me.
\vs{9}Remember, I beseech thee, that thou hast made me as the clay; and wilt thou bring me into dust again?
\vs{10}Hast thou not poured me out as milk, and curdled me like cheese?
\vs{11}Thou hast clothed me with skin and flesh, and hast fenced me with bones and sinews.
\vs{12}Thou hast granted me life and favour, and thy visitation hath preserved my spirit.
\vs{13}And these things hast thou hid in thine heart: I know that this is with thee.
\vs{14}If I sin, then thou markest me, and thou wilt not acquit me from mine iniquity.
\vs{15}If I be wicked, woe unto me; and if I be righteous, yet will I not lift up my head. I am full of confusion; therefore see thou mine affliction;
\vs{16}For it increaseth. Thou huntest me as a fierce lion: and again thou shewest thyself marvellous upon me.
\vs{17}Thou renewest thy witnesses against me, and increasest thine indignation upon me; changes and war are against me.
\vs{18}Wherefore then hast thou brought me forth out of the womb? Oh that I had given up the ghost, and no eye had seen me!
\vs{19}I should have been as though I had not been; I should have been carried from the womb to the grave.
\vs{20}Are not my days few? cease then, and let me alone, that I may take comfort a little,
\vs{21}Before I go whence I shall not return, even to the land of darkness and the shadow of death;
\vs{22}A land of darkness, as darkness itself; and of the shadow of death, without any order, and where the light is as darkness.
\end{scripture}
:::


##### Chapter 11

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="11">
<p><span class="drop-cap">T</span>hen answered Zophar the Naamathite, and said, <span class="verse-number">2</span> Should not the multitude of words be answered? and should a man full of talk be justified? <span class="verse-number">3</span> Should thy lies make men hold their peace? and when thou mockest, shall no man make thee ashamed? <span class="verse-number">4</span> For thou hast said, My doctrine is pure, and I am clean in thine eyes. <span class="verse-number">5</span> But oh that God would speak, and open his lips against thee; <span class="verse-number">6</span> And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is! Know therefore that God exacteth of thee less than thine iniquity deserveth. <span class="verse-number">7</span> Canst thou by searching find out God? canst thou find out the Almighty unto perfection? <span class="verse-number">8</span> It is as high as heaven; what canst thou do? deeper than hell; what canst thou know? <span class="verse-number">9</span> The measure thereof is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea. <span class="verse-number">10</span> If he cut off, and shut up, or gather together, then who can hinder him? <span class="verse-number">11</span> For he knoweth vain men: he seeth wickedness also; will he not then consider it? <span class="verse-number">12</span> For vain men would be wise, though man be born like a wild ass's colt. <span class="verse-number">13</span> If thou prepare thine heart, and stretch out thine hands toward him; <span class="verse-number">14</span> If iniquity be in thine hand, put it far away, and let not wickedness dwell in thy tabernacles. <span class="verse-number">15</span> For then shalt thou lift up thy face without spot; yea, thou shalt be stedfast, and shalt not fear: <span class="verse-number">16</span> Because thou shalt forget thy misery, and remember it as waters that pass away: <span class="verse-number">17</span> And thine age shall be clearer than the noonday: thou shalt shine forth, thou shalt be as the morning. <span class="verse-number">18</span> And thou shalt be secure, because there is hope; yea, thou shalt dig about thee, and thou shalt take thy rest in safety. <span class="verse-number">19</span> Also thou shalt lie down, and none shall make thee afraid; yea, many shall make suit unto thee. <span class="verse-number">20</span> But the eyes of the wicked shall fail, and they shall not escape, and their hope shall be as the giving up of the ghost.</p>
</div>
:::

##### Chapter 12

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="12">
<p><span class="drop-cap">A</span>nd Job answered and said, <span class="verse-number">2</span> No doubt but ye are the people, and wisdom shall die with you. <span class="verse-number">3</span> But I have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you: yea, who knoweth not such things as these? <span class="verse-number">4</span> I am as one mocked of his neighbour, who calleth upon God, and he answereth him: the just upright man is laughed to scorn. <span class="verse-number">5</span> He that is ready to slip with his feet is as a lamp despised in the thought of him that is at ease. <span class="verse-number">6</span> The tabernacles of robbers prosper, and they that provoke God are secure; into whose hand God bringeth abundantly. <span class="verse-number">7</span> But ask now the beasts, and they shall teach thee; and the fowls of the air, and they shall tell thee: <span class="verse-number">8</span> Or speak to the earth, and it shall teach thee: and the fishes of the sea shall declare unto thee. <span class="verse-number">9</span> Who knoweth not in all these that the hand of the LORD hath wrought this? <span class="verse-number">10</span> In whose hand is the soul of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind. <span class="verse-number">11</span> Doth not the ear try words? and the mouth taste his meat? <span class="verse-number">12</span> With the ancient is wisdom; and in length of days understanding. <span class="verse-number">13</span> With him is wisdom and strength, he hath counsel and understanding. <span class="verse-number">14</span> Behold, he breaketh down, and it cannot be built again: he shutteth up a man, and there can be no opening. <span class="verse-number">15</span> Behold, he withholdeth the waters, and they dry up: also he sendeth them out, and they overturn the earth. <span class="verse-number">16</span> With him is strength and wisdom: the deceived and the deceiver are his. <span class="verse-number">17</span> He leadeth counsellors away spoiled, and maketh the judges fools. <span class="verse-number">18</span> He looseth the bond of kings, and girdeth their loins with a girdle. <span class="verse-number">19</span> He leadeth princes away spoiled, and overthroweth the mighty. <span class="verse-number">20</span> He removeth away the speech of the trusty, and taketh away the understanding of the aged. <span class="verse-number">21</span> He poureth contempt upon princes, and weakeneth the strength of the mighty. <span class="verse-number">22</span> He discovereth deep things out of darkness, and bringeth out to light the shadow of death. <span class="verse-number">23</span> He increaseth the nations, and destroyeth them: he enlargeth the nations, and straiteneth them again. <span class="verse-number">24</span> He taketh away the heart of the chief of the people of the earth, and causeth them to wander in a wilderness where there is no way. <span class="verse-number">25</span> They grope in the dark without light, and he maketh them to stagger like a drunken man.</p>
</div>
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
\begin{scripture}[Job][12]
\lettrine[lines=4]{A}{nd} Job answered and said,
\vs{2}No doubt but ye are the people, and wisdom shall die with you.
\vs{3}But I have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you: yea, who knoweth not such things as these?
\vs{4}I am as one mocked of his neighbour, who calleth upon God, and he answereth him: the just upright man is laughed to scorn.
\vs{5}He that is ready to slip with his feet is as a lamp despised in the thought of him that is at ease.
\vs{6}The tabernacles of robbers prosper, and they that provoke God are secure; into whose hand God bringeth abundantly.
\vs{7}But ask now the beasts, and they shall teach thee; and the fowls of the air, and they shall tell thee:
\vs{8}Or speak to the earth, and it shall teach thee: and the fishes of the sea shall declare unto thee.
\vs{9}Who knoweth not in all these that the hand of the LORD hath wrought this?
\vs{10}In whose hand is the soul of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind.
\vs{11}Doth not the ear try words? and the mouth taste his meat?
\vs{12}With the ancient is wisdom; and in length of days understanding.
\vs{13}With him is wisdom and strength, he hath counsel and understanding.
\vs{14}Behold, he breaketh down, and it cannot be built again: he shutteth up a man, and there can be no opening.
\vs{15}Behold, he withholdeth the waters, and they dry up: also he sendeth them out, and they overturn the earth.
\vs{16}With him is strength and wisdom: the deceived and the deceiver are his.
\vs{17}He leadeth counsellors away spoiled, and maketh the judges fools.
\vs{18}He looseth the bond of kings, and girdeth their loins with a girdle.
\vs{19}He leadeth princes away spoiled, and overthroweth the mighty.
\vs{20}He removeth away the speech of the trusty, and taketh away the understanding of the aged.
\vs{21}He poureth contempt upon princes, and weakeneth the strength of the mighty.
\vs{22}He discovereth deep things out of darkness, and bringeth out to light the shadow of death.
\vs{23}He increaseth the nations, and destroyeth them: he enlargeth the nations, and straiteneth them again.
\vs{24}He taketh away the heart of the chief of the people of the earth, and causeth them to wander in a wilderness where there is no way.
\vs{25}They grope in the dark without light, and he maketh them to stagger like a drunken man.
\end{scripture}
:::


##### Chapter 13

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="13">
<p><span class="drop-cap">L</span>o, mine eye hath seen all this, mine ear hath heard and understood it. <span class="verse-number">2</span> What ye know, the same do I know also: I am not inferior unto you. <span class="verse-number">3</span> Surely I would speak to the Almighty, and I desire to reason with God. <span class="verse-number">4</span> But ye are forgers of lies, ye are all physicians of no value. <span class="verse-number">5</span> O that ye would altogether hold your peace! and it should be your wisdom. <span class="verse-number">6</span> Hear now my reasoning, and hearken to the pleadings of my lips. <span class="verse-number">7</span> Will ye speak wickedly for God? and talk deceitfully for him? <span class="verse-number">8</span> Will ye accept his person? will ye contend for God? <span class="verse-number">9</span> Is it good that he should search you out? or as one man mocketh another, do ye so mock him? <span class="verse-number">10</span> He will surely reprove you, if ye do secretly accept persons. <span class="verse-number">11</span> Shall not his excellency make you afraid? and his dread fall upon you? <span class="verse-number">12</span> Your remembrances are like unto ashes, your bodies to bodies of clay. <span class="verse-number">13</span> Hold your peace, let me alone, that I may speak, and let come on me what will. <span class="verse-number">14</span> Wherefore do I take my flesh in my teeth, and put my life in mine hand? <span class="verse-number">15</span> Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him: but I will maintain mine own ways before him. <span class="verse-number">16</span> He also shall be my salvation: for an hypocrite shall not come before him. <span class="verse-number">17</span> Hear diligently my speech, and my declaration with your ears. <span class="verse-number">18</span> Behold now, I have ordered my cause; I know that I shall be justified. <span class="verse-number">19</span> Who is he that will plead with me? for now, if I hold my tongue, I shall give up the ghost. <span class="verse-number">20</span> Only do not two things unto me: then will I not hide myself from thee. <span class="verse-number">21</span> Withdraw thine hand far from me: and let not thy dread make me afraid. <span class="verse-number">22</span> Then call thou, and I will answer: or let me speak, and answer thou me. <span class="verse-number">23</span> How many are mine iniquities and sins? make me to know my transgression and my sin. <span class="verse-number">24</span> Wherefore hidest thou thy face, and holdest me for thine enemy? <span class="verse-number">25</span> Wilt thou break a leaf driven to and fro? and wilt thou pursue the dry stubble? <span class="verse-number">26</span> For thou writest bitter things against me, and makest me to possess the iniquities of my youth. <span class="verse-number">27</span> Thou puttest my feet also in the stocks, and lookest narrowly unto all my paths; thou settest a print upon the heels of my feet. <span class="verse-number">28</span> And he, as a rotten thing, consumeth, as a garment that is moth eaten.</p>
</div>
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
\begin{scripture}[Job][13]
\lettrine[lines=4]{L}{o,} mine eye hath seen all this, mine ear hath heard and understood it.
\vs{2}What ye know, the same do I know also: I am not inferior unto you.
\vs{3}Surely I would speak to the Almighty, and I desire to reason with God.
\vs{4}But ye are forgers of lies, ye are all physicians of no value.
\vs{5}O that ye would altogether hold your peace! and it should be your wisdom.
\vs{6}Hear now my reasoning, and hearken to the pleadings of my lips.
\vs{7}Will ye speak wickedly for God? and talk deceitfully for him?
\vs{8}Will ye accept his person? will ye contend for God?
\vs{9}Is it good that he should search you out? or as one man mocketh another, do ye so mock him?
\vs{10}He will surely reprove you, if ye do secretly accept persons.
\vs{11}Shall not his excellency make you afraid? and his dread fall upon you?
\vs{12}Your remembrances are like unto ashes, your bodies to bodies of clay.
\vs{13}Hold your peace, let me alone, that I may speak, and let come on me what will.
\vs{14}Wherefore do I take my flesh in my teeth, and put my life in mine hand?
\vs{15}Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him: but I will maintain mine own ways before him.
\vs{16}He also shall be my salvation: for an hypocrite shall not come before him.
\vs{17}Hear diligently my speech, and my declaration with your ears.
\vs{18}Behold now, I have ordered my cause; I know that I shall be justified.
\vs{19}Who is he that will plead with me? for now, if I hold my tongue, I shall give up the ghost.
\vs{20}Only do not two things unto me: then will I not hide myself from thee.
\vs{21}Withdraw thine hand far from me: and let not thy dread make me afraid.
\vs{22}Then call thou, and I will answer: or let me speak, and answer thou me.
\vs{23}How many are mine iniquities and sins? make me to know my transgression and my sin.
\vs{24}Wherefore hidest thou thy face, and holdest me for thine enemy?
\vs{25}Wilt thou break a leaf driven to and fro? and wilt thou pursue the dry stubble?
\vs{26}For thou writest bitter things against me, and makest me to possess the iniquities of my youth.
\vs{27}Thou puttest my feet also in the stocks, and lookest narrowly unto all my paths; thou settest a print upon the heels of my feet.
\vs{28}And he, as a rotten thing, consumeth, as a garment that is moth eaten.
\end{scripture}
:::


##### Chapter 14

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="14">
<p><span class="drop-cap">M</span>an that is born of a woman is of few days and full of trouble. <span class="verse-number">2</span> He cometh forth like a flower, and is cut down: he fleeth also as a shadow, and continueth not. <span class="verse-number">3</span> And doth thou open thine eyes upon such an one, and bringest me into judgment with thee? <span class="verse-number">4</span> Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? not one. <span class="verse-number">5</span> Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months are with thee, thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass; <span class="verse-number">6</span> Turn from him, that he may rest, till he shall accomplish, as an hireling, his day. <span class="verse-number">7</span> For there is hope of a tree, if it be cut down, that it will sprout again, and that the tender branch thereof will not cease. <span class="verse-number">8</span> Though the root thereof wax old in the earth, and the stock thereof die in the ground; <span class="verse-number">9</span> Yet through the scent of water it will bud, and bring forth boughs like a plant. <span class="verse-number">10</span> But man dieth, and wasteth away: yea, man giveth up the ghost, and where is he? <span class="verse-number">11</span> As the waters fail from the sea, and the flood decayeth and drieth up: <span class="verse-number">12</span> So man lieth down, and riseth not: till the heavens be no more, they shall not awake, nor be raised out of their sleep. <span class="verse-number">13</span> O that thou wouldest hide me in the grave, that thou wouldest keep me secret, until thy wrath be past, that thou wouldest appoint me a set time, and remember me! <span class="verse-number">14</span> If a man die, shall he live again? all the days of my appointed time will I wait, till my change come. <span class="verse-number">15</span> Thou shalt call, and I will answer thee: thou wilt have a desire to the work of thine hands. <span class="verse-number">16</span> For now thou numberest my steps: dost thou not watch over my sin? <span class="verse-number">17</span> My transgression is sealed up in a bag, and thou sewest up mine iniquity. <span class="verse-number">18</span> And surely the mountains falling cometh to nought, and the rock is removed out of his place. <span class="verse-number">19</span> The waters wear the stones: thou washest away the things which grow out of the dust of the earth; and thou destroyest the hope of man. <span class="verse-number">20</span> Thou prevailest for ever against him, and he passeth: thou changest his countenance, and sendest him away. <span class="verse-number">21</span> His sons come to honour, and he knoweth it not; and they are brought low, but he perceiveth it not of them. <span class="verse-number">22</span> But his flesh upon him shall have pain, and his soul within him shall mourn.</p>
</div>
:::

##### Chapter 15

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="15">
<p><span class="drop-cap">T</span>hen answered Eliphaz the Temanite, and said, <span class="verse-number">2</span> Should a wise man utter vain knowledge, and fill his belly with the east wind? <span class="verse-number">3</span> Should he reason with unprofitable talk? or with speeches wherewith he can do no good? <span class="verse-number">4</span> Yea, thou castest off fear, and restrainest prayer before God. <span class="verse-number">5</span> For thy mouth uttereth thine iniquity, and thou choosest the tongue of the crafty. <span class="verse-number">6</span> Thine own mouth condemneth thee, and not I: yea, thine own lips testify against thee. <span class="verse-number">7</span> Art thou the first man that was born? or wast thou made before the hills? <span class="verse-number">8</span> Hast thou heard the secret of God? and dost thou restrain wisdom to thyself? <span class="verse-number">9</span> What knowest thou, that we know not? what understandest thou, which is not in us? <span class="verse-number">10</span> With us are both the grayheaded and very aged men, much elder than thy father. <span class="verse-number">11</span> Are the consolations of God small with thee? is there any secret thing with thee? <span class="verse-number">12</span> Why doth thine heart carry thee away? and what do thy eyes wink at, <span class="verse-number">13</span> That thou turnest thy spirit against God, and lettest such words go out of thy mouth? <span class="verse-number">14</span> What is man, that he should be clean? and he which is born of a woman, that he should be righteous? <span class="verse-number">15</span> Behold, he putteth no trust in his saints; yea, the heavens are not clean in his sight. <span class="verse-number">16</span> How much more abominable and filthy is man, which drinketh iniquity like water? <span class="verse-number">17</span> I will shew thee, hear me; and that which I have seen I will declare; <span class="verse-number">18</span> Which wise men have told from their fathers, and have not hid it: <span class="verse-number">19</span> Unto whom alone the earth was given, and no stranger passed among them. <span class="verse-number">20</span> The wicked man travaileth with pain all his days, and the number of years is hidden to the oppressor. <span class="verse-number">21</span> A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him. <span class="verse-number">22</span> He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword. <span class="verse-number">23</span> He wandereth abroad for bread, saying, Where is it? he knoweth that the day of darkness is ready at his hand. <span class="verse-number">24</span> Trouble and anguish shall make him afraid; they shall prevail against him, as a king ready to the battle. <span class="verse-number">25</span> For he stretcheth out his hand against God, and strengtheneth himself against the Almighty. <span class="verse-number">26</span> He runneth upon him, even on his neck, upon the thick bosses of his bucklers: <span class="verse-number">27</span> Because he covereth his face with his fatness, and maketh collops of fat on his flanks. <span class="verse-number">28</span> And he dwelleth in desolate cities, and in houses which no man inhabiteth, which are ready to become heaps. <span class="verse-number">29</span> He shall not be rich, neither shall his substance continue, neither shall he prolong the perfection thereof upon the earth. <span class="verse-number">30</span> He shall not depart out of darkness; the flame shall dry up his branches, and by the breath of his mouth shall he go away. <span class="verse-number">31</span> Let not him that is deceived trust in vanity: for vanity shall be his recompence. <span class="verse-number">32</span> It shall be accomplished before his time, and his branch shall not be green. <span class="verse-number">33</span> He shall shake off his unripe grape as the vine, and shall cast off his flower as the olive. <span class="verse-number">34</span> For the congregation of hypocrites shall be desolate, and fire shall consume the tabernacles of bribery. <span class="verse-number">35</span> They conceive mischief, and bring forth vanity, and their belly prepareth deceit.</p>
</div>
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
\begin{scripture}[Job][15]
\lettrine[lines=4]{T}{hen} answered Eliphaz the Temanite, and said,
\vs{2}Should a wise man utter vain knowledge, and fill his belly with the east wind?
\vs{3}Should he reason with unprofitable talk? or with speeches wherewith he can do no good?
\vs{4}Yea, thou castest off fear, and restrainest prayer before God.
\vs{5}For thy mouth uttereth thine iniquity, and thou choosest the tongue of the crafty.
\vs{6}Thine own mouth condemneth thee, and not I: yea, thine own lips testify against thee.
\vs{7}Art thou the first man that was born? or wast thou made before the hills?
\vs{8}Hast thou heard the secret of God? and dost thou restrain wisdom to thyself?
\vs{9}What knowest thou, that we know not? what understandest thou, which is not in us?
\vs{10}With us are both the grayheaded and very aged men, much elder than thy father.
\vs{11}Are the consolations of God small with thee? is there any secret thing with thee?
\vs{12}Why doth thine heart carry thee away? and what do thy eyes wink at,
\vs{13}That thou turnest thy spirit against God, and lettest such words go out of thy mouth?
\vs{14}What is man, that he should be clean? and he which is born of a woman, that he should be righteous?
\vs{15}Behold, he putteth no trust in his saints; yea, the heavens are not clean in his sight.
\vs{16}How much more abominable and filthy is man, which drinketh iniquity like water?
\vs{17}I will shew thee, hear me; and that which I have seen I will declare;
\vs{18}Which wise men have told from their fathers, and have not hid it:
\vs{19}Unto whom alone the earth was given, and no stranger passed among them.
\vs{20}The wicked man travaileth with pain all his days, and the number of years is hidden to the oppressor.
\vs{21}A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him.
\vs{22}He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword.
\vs{23}He wandereth abroad for bread, saying, Where is it? he knoweth that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.
\vs{24}Trouble and anguish shall make him afraid; they shall prevail against him, as a king ready to the battle.
\vs{25}For he stretcheth out his hand against God, and strengtheneth himself against the Almighty.
\vs{26}He runneth upon him, even on his neck, upon the thick bosses of his bucklers:
\vs{27}Because he covereth his face with his fatness, and maketh collops of fat on his flanks.
\vs{28}And he dwelleth in desolate cities, and in houses which no man inhabiteth, which are ready to become heaps.
\vs{29}He shall not be rich, neither shall his substance continue, neither shall he prolong the perfection thereof upon the earth.
\vs{30}He shall not depart out of darkness; the flame shall dry up his branches, and by the breath of his mouth shall he go away.
\vs{31}Let not him that is deceived trust in vanity: for vanity shall be his recompence.
\vs{32}It shall be accomplished before his time, and his branch shall not be green.
\vs{33}He shall shake off his unripe grape as the vine, and shall cast off his flower as the olive.
\vs{34}For the congregation of hypocrites shall be desolate, and fire shall consume the tabernacles of bribery.
\vs{35}They conceive mischief, and bring forth vanity, and their belly prepareth deceit.
\end{scripture}
:::


##### Chapter 16

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="16">
<p><span class="drop-cap">T</span>hen Job answered and said, <span class="verse-number">2</span> I have heard many such things: miserable comforters are ye all. <span class="verse-number">3</span> Shall vain words have an end? or what emboldeneth thee that thou answerest? <span class="verse-number">4</span> I also could speak as ye do: if your soul were in my soul's stead, I could heap up words against you, and shake mine head at you. <span class="verse-number">5</span> But I would strengthen you with my mouth, and the moving of my lips should asswage your grief. <span class="verse-number">6</span> Though I speak, my grief is not asswaged: and though I forbear, what am I eased? <span class="verse-number">7</span> But now he hath made me weary: thou hast made desolate all my company. <span class="verse-number">8</span> And thou hast filled me with wrinkles, which is a witness against me: and my leanness rising up in me beareth witness to my face. <span class="verse-number">9</span> He teareth me in his wrath, who hateth me: he gnasheth upon me with his teeth; mine enemy sharpeneth his eyes upon me. <span class="verse-number">10</span> They have gaped upon me with their mouth; they have smitten me upon the cheek reproachfully; they have gathered themselves together against me. <span class="verse-number">11</span> God hath delivered me to the ungodly, and turned me over into the hands of the wicked. <span class="verse-number">12</span> I was at ease, but he hath broken me asunder: he hath also taken me by my neck, and shaken me to pieces, and set me up for his mark. <span class="verse-number">13</span> His archers compass me round about, he cleaveth my reins asunder, and doth not spare; he poureth out my gall upon the ground. <span class="verse-number">14</span> He breaketh me with breach upon breach, he runneth upon me like a giant. <span class="verse-number">15</span> I have sewed sackcloth upon my skin, and defiled my horn in the dust. <span class="verse-number">16</span> My face is foul with weeping, and on my eyelids is the shadow of death; <span class="verse-number">17</span> Not for any injustice in mine hands: also my prayer is pure. <span class="verse-number">18</span> O earth, cover not thou my blood, and let my cry have no place. <span class="verse-number">19</span> Also now, behold, my witness is in heaven, and my record is on high. <span class="verse-number">20</span> My friends scorn me: but mine eye poureth out tears unto God. <span class="verse-number">21</span> O that one might plead for a man with God, as a man pleadeth for his neighbour! <span class="verse-number">22</span> When a few years are come, then I shall go the way whence I shall not return.</p>
</div>
:::
