##### Chapter 17

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="17">
<p><span class="drop-cap">M</span>y breath is corrupt, my days are extinct, the graves are ready for me. <span class="verse-number">2</span> Are there not mockers with me? and doth not mine eye continue in their provocation? <span class="verse-number">3</span> Lay down now, put me in a surety with thee; who is he that will strike hands with me? <span class="verse-number">4</span> For thou hast hid their heart from understanding: therefore shalt thou not exalt them. <span class="verse-number">5</span> He that speaketh flattery to his friends, even the eyes of his children shall fail. <span class="verse-number">6</span> He hath made me also a byword of the people; and aforetime I was as a tabret. <span class="verse-number">7</span> Mine eye also is dim by reason of sorrow, and all my members are as a shadow. <span class="verse-number">8</span> Upright men shall be astonied at this, and the innocent shall stir up himself against the hypocrite. <span class="verse-number">9</span> The righteous also shall hold on his way, and he that hath clean hands shall be stronger and stronger. <span class="verse-number">10</span> But as for you all, do ye return, and come now: for I cannot find one wise man among you. <span class="verse-number">11</span> My days are past, my purposes are broken off, even the thoughts of my heart. <span class="verse-number">12</span> They change the night into day: the light is short because of darkness. <span class="verse-number">13</span> If I wait, the grave is mine house: I have made my bed in the darkness. <span class="verse-number">14</span> I have said to corruption, Thou art my father: to the worm, Thou art my mother, and my sister. <span class="verse-number">15</span> And where is now my hope? as for my hope, who shall see it? <span class="verse-number">16</span> They shall go down to the bars of the pit, when our rest together is in the dust.</p>
</div>
:::

##### Chapter 18

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="18">
<p><span class="drop-cap">T</span>hen answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said, <span class="verse-number">2</span> How long will it be ere ye make an end of words? mark, and afterwards we will speak. <span class="verse-number">3</span> Wherefore are we counted as beasts, and reputed vile in your sight? <span class="verse-number">4</span> He teareth himself in his anger: shall the earth be forsaken for thee? and shall the rock be removed out of his place? <span class="verse-number">5</span> Yea, the light of the wicked shall be put out, and the spark of his fire shall not shine. <span class="verse-number">6</span> The light shall be dark in his tabernacle, and his candle shall be put out with him. <span class="verse-number">7</span> The steps of his strength shall be straitened, and his own counsel shall cast him down. <span class="verse-number">8</span> For he is cast into a net by his own feet, and he walketh upon a snare. <span class="verse-number">9</span> The gin shall take him by the heel, and the robber shall prevail against him. <span class="verse-number">10</span> The snare is laid for him in the ground, and a trap for him in the way. <span class="verse-number">11</span> Terrors shall make him afraid on every side, and shall drive him to his feet. <span class="verse-number">12</span> His strength shall be hungerbitten, and destruction shall be ready at his side. <span class="verse-number">13</span> It shall devour the strength of his skin: even the firstborn of death shall devour his strength. <span class="verse-number">14</span> His confidence shall be rooted out of his tabernacle, and it shall bring him to the king of terrors. <span class="verse-number">15</span> It shall dwell in his tabernacle, because it is none of his: brimstone shall be scattered upon his habitation. <span class="verse-number">16</span> His roots shall be dried up beneath, and above shall his branch be cut off. <span class="verse-number">17</span> His remembrance shall perish from the earth, and he shall have no name in the street. <span class="verse-number">18</span> He shall be driven from light into darkness, and chased out of the world. <span class="verse-number">19</span> He shall neither have son nor nephew among his people, nor any remaining in his dwellings. <span class="verse-number">20</span> They that come after him shall be astonied at his day, as they that went before were affrighted. <span class="verse-number">21</span> Surely such are the dwellings of the wicked, and this is the place of him that knoweth not God.</p>
</div>
:::

##### Chapter 19

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="19">
<p><span class="drop-cap">T</span>hen Job answered and said, <span class="verse-number">2</span> How long will ye vex my soul, and break me in pieces with words? <span class="verse-number">3</span> These ten times have ye reproached me: ye are not ashamed that ye make yourselves strange to me. <span class="verse-number">4</span> And be it indeed that I have erred, mine error remaineth with myself. <span class="verse-number">5</span> If indeed ye will magnify yourselves against me, and plead against me my reproach: <span class="verse-number">6</span> Know now that God hath overthrown me, and hath compassed me with his net. <span class="verse-number">7</span> Behold, I cry out of wrong, but I am not heard: I cry aloud, but there is no judgment. <span class="verse-number">8</span> He hath fenced up my way that I cannot pass, and he hath set darkness in my paths. <span class="verse-number">9</span> He hath stripped me of my glory, and taken the crown from my head. <span class="verse-number">10</span> He hath destroyed me on every side, and I am gone: and mine hope hath he removed like a tree. <span class="verse-number">11</span> He hath also kindled his wrath against me, and he counteth me unto him as one of his enemies. <span class="verse-number">12</span> His troops come together, and raise up their way against me, and encamp round about my tabernacle. <span class="verse-number">13</span> He hath put my brethren far from me, and mine acquaintance are verily estranged from me. <span class="verse-number">14</span> My kinsfolk have failed, and my familiar friends have forgotten me. <span class="verse-number">15</span> They that dwell in mine house, and my maids, count me for a stranger: I am an alien in their sight. <span class="verse-number">16</span> I called my servant, and he gave me no answer; I intreated him with my mouth. <span class="verse-number">17</span> My breath is strange to my wife, though I intreated for the children's sake of mine own body. <span class="verse-number">18</span> Yea, young children despised me; I arose, and they spake against me. <span class="verse-number">19</span> All my inward friends abhorred me: and they whom I loved are turned against me. <span class="verse-number">20</span> My bone cleaveth to my skin and to my flesh, and I am escaped with the skin of my teeth. <span class="verse-number">21</span> Have pity upon me, have pity upon me, O ye my friends; for the hand of God hath touched me. <span class="verse-number">22</span> Why do ye persecute me as God, and are not satisfied with my flesh? <span class="verse-number">23</span> Oh that my words were now written! oh that they were printed in a book! <span class="verse-number">24</span> That they were graven with an iron pen and lead in the rock for ever! <span class="verse-number">25</span> For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth: <span class="verse-number">26</span> And though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God: <span class="verse-number">27</span> Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another; though my reins be consumed within me. <span class="verse-number">28</span> But ye should say, Why persecute we him, seeing the root of the matter is found in me? <span class="verse-number">29</span> Be ye afraid of the sword: for wrath bringeth the punishments of the sword, that ye may know there is a judgment.</p>
</div>
:::

##### Chapter 20

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="20">
<p><span class="drop-cap">T</span>hen answered Zophar the Naamathite, and said, <span class="verse-number">2</span> Therefore do my thoughts cause me to answer, and for this I make haste. <span class="verse-number">3</span> I have heard the check of my reproach, and the spirit of my understanding causeth me to answer. <span class="verse-number">4</span> Knowest thou not this of old, since man was placed upon earth, <span class="verse-number">5</span> That the triumphing of the wicked is short, and the joy of the hypocrite but for a moment? <span class="verse-number">6</span> Though his excellency mount up to the heavens, and his head reach unto the clouds; <span class="verse-number">7</span> Yet he shall perish for ever like his own dung: they which have seen him shall say, Where is he? <span class="verse-number">8</span> He shall fly away as a dream, and shall not be found: yea, he shall be chased away as a vision of the night. <span class="verse-number">9</span> The eye also which saw him shall see him no more; neither shall his place any more behold him. <span class="verse-number">10</span> His children shall seek to please the poor, and his hands shall restore their goods. <span class="verse-number">11</span> His bones are full of the sin of his youth, which shall lie down with him in the dust. <span class="verse-number">12</span> Though wickedness be sweet in his mouth, though he hide it under his tongue; <span class="verse-number">13</span> Though he spare it, and forsake it not; but keep it still within his mouth: <span class="verse-number">14</span> Yet his meat in his bowels is turned, it is the gall of asps within him. <span class="verse-number">15</span> He hath swallowed down riches, and he shall vomit them up again: God shall cast them out of his belly. <span class="verse-number">16</span> He shall suck the poison of asps: the viper's tongue shall slay him. <span class="verse-number">17</span> He shall not see the rivers, the floods, the brooks of honey and butter. <span class="verse-number">18</span> That which he laboured for shall he restore, and shall not swallow it down: according to his substance shall the restitution be, and he shall not rejoice therein. <span class="verse-number">19</span> Because he hath oppressed and hath forsaken the poor; because he hath violently taken away an house which he builded not; <span class="verse-number">20</span> Surely he shall not feel quietness in his belly, he shall not save of that which he desired. <span class="verse-number">21</span> There shall none of his meat be left; therefore shall no man look for his goods. <span class="verse-number">22</span> In the fulness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits: every hand of the wicked shall come upon him. <span class="verse-number">23</span> When he is about to fill his belly, God shall cast the fury of his wrath upon him, and shall rain it upon him while he is eating. <span class="verse-number">24</span> He shall flee from the iron weapon, and the bow of steel shall strike him through. <span class="verse-number">25</span> It is drawn, and cometh out of the body; yea, the glittering sword cometh out of his gall: terrors are upon him. <span class="verse-number">26</span> All darkness shall be hid in his secret places: a fire not blown shall consume him; it shall go ill with him that is left in his tabernacle. <span class="verse-number">27</span> The heaven shall reveal his iniquity; and the earth shall rise up against him. <span class="verse-number">28</span> The increase of his house shall depart, and his goods shall flow away in the day of his wrath. <span class="verse-number">29</span> This is the portion of a wicked man from God, and the heritage appointed unto him by God.</p>
</div>
:::

\vs{15}He hath swallowed down riches, and he shall vomit them up again: God shall cast them out of his belly.
\vs{16}He shall suck the poison of asps: the viper's tongue shall slay him.
\vs{17}He shall not see the rivers, the floods, the brooks of honey and butter.
\vs{18}That which he laboured for shall he restore, and shall not swallow it down: according to his substance shall the restitution be, and he shall not rejoice therein.
\vs{19}Because he hath oppressed and hath forsaken the poor; because he hath violently taken away an house which he builded not;
\vs{20}Surely he shall not feel quietness in his belly, he shall not save of that which he desired.
\vs{21}There shall none of his meat be left; therefore shall no man look for his goods.
\vs{22}In the fulness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits: every hand of the wicked shall come upon him.
\vs{23}When he is about to fill his belly, God shall cast the fury of his wrath upon him, and shall rain it upon him while he is eating.
\vs{24}He shall flee from the iron weapon, and the bow of steel shall strike him through.
\vs{25}It is drawn, and cometh out of the body; yea, the glittering sword cometh out of his gall: terrors are upon him.
\vs{26}All darkness shall be hid in his secret places: a fire not blown shall consume him; it shall go ill with him that is left in his tabernacle.
\vs{27}The heaven shall reveal his iniquity; and the earth shall rise up against him.
\vs{28}The increase of his house shall depart, and his goods shall flow away in the day of his wrath.
\vs{29}This is the portion of a wicked man from God, and the heritage appointed unto him by God.
\end{scripture}
:::


##### Chapter 21

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="21">
<p><span class="drop-cap">B</span>ut Job answered and said, <span class="verse-number">2</span> Hear diligently my speech, and let this be your consolations. <span class="verse-number">3</span> Suffer me that I may speak; and after that I have spoken, mock on. <span class="verse-number">4</span> As for me, is my complaint to man? and if it were so, why should not my spirit be troubled? <span class="verse-number">5</span> Mark me, and be astonished, and lay your hand upon your mouth. <span class="verse-number">6</span> Even when I remember I am afraid, and trembling taketh hold on my flesh. <span class="verse-number">7</span> Wherefore do the wicked live, become old, yea, are mighty in power? <span class="verse-number">8</span> Their seed is established in their sight with them, and their offspring before their eyes. <span class="verse-number">9</span> Their houses are safe from fear, neither is the rod of God upon them. <span class="verse-number">10</span> Their bull gendereth, and faileth not; their cow calveth, and casteth not her calf. <span class="verse-number">11</span> They send forth their little ones like a flock, and their children dance. <span class="verse-number">12</span> They take the timbrel and harp, and rejoice at the sound of the organ. <span class="verse-number">13</span> They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment go down to the grave. <span class="verse-number">14</span> Therefore they say unto God, Depart from us; for we desire not the knowledge of thy ways. <span class="verse-number">15</span> What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? and what profit should we have, if we pray unto him? <span class="verse-number">16</span> Lo, their good is not in their hand: the counsel of the wicked is far from me. <span class="verse-number">17</span> How oft is the candle of the wicked put out! and how oft cometh their destruction upon them! God distributeth sorrows in his anger. <span class="verse-number">18</span> They are as stubble before the wind, and as chaff that the storm carrieth away. <span class="verse-number">19</span> God layeth up his iniquity for his children: he rewardeth him, and he shall know it. <span class="verse-number">20</span> His eyes shall see his destruction, and he shall drink of the wrath of the Almighty. <span class="verse-number">21</span> For what pleasure hath he in his house after him, when the number of his months is cut off in the midst? <span class="verse-number">22</span> Shall any teach God knowledge? seeing he judgeth those that are high. <span class="verse-number">23</span> One dieth in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet. <span class="verse-number">24</span> His breasts are full of milk, and his bones are moistened with marrow. <span class="verse-number">25</span> And another dieth in the bitterness of his soul, and never eateth with pleasure. <span class="verse-number">26</span> They shall lie down alike in the dust, and the worms shall cover them. <span class="verse-number">27</span> Behold, I know your thoughts, and the devices which ye wrongfully imagine against me. <span class="verse-number">28</span> For ye say, Where is the house of the prince? and where are the dwelling places of the wicked? <span class="verse-number">29</span> Have ye not asked them that go by the way? and do ye not know their tokens, <span class="verse-number">30</span> That the wicked is reserved to the day of destruction? they shall be brought forth to the day of wrath. <span class="verse-number">31</span> Who shall declare his way to his face? and who shall repay him what he hath done? <span class="verse-number">32</span> Yet shall he be brought to the grave, and shall remain in the tomb. <span class="verse-number">33</span> The clods of the valley shall be sweet unto him, and every man shall draw after him, as there are innumerable before him. <span class="verse-number">34</span> How then comfort ye me in vain, seeing in your answers there remaineth falsehood?</p>
</div>
:::

##### Chapter 22

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="22">
<p><span class="drop-cap">T</span>hen Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said, <span class="verse-number">2</span> Can a man be profitable unto God, as he that is wise may be profitable unto himself? <span class="verse-number">3</span> Is it any pleasure to the Almighty, that thou art righteous? or is it gain to him, that thou makest thy ways perfect? <span class="verse-number">4</span> Will he reprove thee for fear of thee? will he enter with thee into judgment? <span class="verse-number">5</span> Is not thy wickedness great? and thine iniquities infinite? <span class="verse-number">6</span> For thou hast taken a pledge from thy brother for nought, and stripped the naked of their clothing. <span class="verse-number">7</span> Thou hast not given water to the weary to drink, and thou hast withholden bread from the hungry. <span class="verse-number">8</span> But as for the mighty man, he had the earth; and the honourable man dwelt in it. <span class="verse-number">9</span> Thou hast sent widows away empty, and the arms of the fatherless have been broken. <span class="verse-number">10</span> Therefore snares are round about thee, and sudden fear troubleth thee; <span class="verse-number">11</span> Or darkness, that thou canst not see; and abundance of waters cover thee. <span class="verse-number">12</span> Is not God in the height of heaven? and behold the height of the stars, how high they are! <span class="verse-number">13</span> And thou sayest, How doth God know? can he judge through the dark cloud? <span class="verse-number">14</span> Thick clouds are a covering to him, that he seeth not; and he walketh in the circuit of heaven. <span class="verse-number">15</span> Hast thou marked the old way which wicked men have trodden? <span class="verse-number">16</span> Which were cut down out of time, whose foundation was overflown with a flood: <span class="verse-number">17</span> Which said unto God, Depart from us: and what can the Almighty do for them? <span class="verse-number">18</span> Yet he filled their houses with good things: but the counsel of the wicked is far from me. <span class="verse-number">19</span> The righteous see it, and are glad: and the innocent laugh them to scorn. <span class="verse-number">20</span> Whereas our substance is not cut down, but the remnant of them the fire consumeth. <span class="verse-number">21</span> Acquaint now thyself with him, and be at peace: thereby good shall come unto thee. <span class="verse-number">22</span> Receive, I pray thee, the law from his mouth, and lay up his words in thine heart. <span class="verse-number">23</span> If thou return to the Almighty, thou shalt be built up, thou shalt put away iniquity far from thy tabernacles. <span class="verse-number">24</span> Then shalt thou lay up gold as dust, and the gold of Ophir as the stones of the brooks. <span class="verse-number">25</span> Yea, the Almighty shall be thy defence, and thou shalt have plenty of silver. <span class="verse-number">26</span> For then shalt thou have thy delight in the Almighty, and shalt lift up thy face unto God. <span class="verse-number">27</span> Thou shalt make thy prayer unto him, and he shall hear thee, and thou shalt pay thy vows. <span class="verse-number">28</span> Thou shalt also decree a thing, and it shall be established unto thee: and the light shall shine upon thy ways. <span class="verse-number">29</span> When men are cast down, then thou shalt say, There is lifting up; and he shall save the humble person. <span class="verse-number">30</span> He shall deliver the island of the innocent: and it is delivered by the pureness of thine hands.</p>
</div>
:::

\vs{7}Thou hast not given water to the weary to drink, and thou hast withholden bread from the hungry.
\vs{8}But as for the mighty man, he had the earth; and the honourable man dwelt in it.
\vs{9}Thou hast sent widows away empty, and the arms of the fatherless have been broken.
\vs{10}Therefore snares are round about thee, and sudden fear troubleth thee;
\vs{11}Or darkness, that thou canst not see; and abundance of waters cover thee.
\vs{12}Is not God in the height of heaven? and behold the height of the stars, how high they are!
\vs{13}And thou sayest, How doth God know? can he judge through the dark cloud?
\vs{14}Thick clouds are a covering to him, that he seeth not; and he walketh in the circuit of heaven.
\vs{15}Hast thou marked the old way which wicked men have trodden?
\vs{16}Which were cut down out of time, whose foundation was overflown with a flood:
\vs{17}Which said unto God, Depart from us: and what can the Almighty do for them?
\vs{18}Yet he filled their houses with good things: but the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
\vs{19}The righteous see it, and are glad: and the innocent laugh them to scorn.
\vs{20}Whereas our substance is not cut down, but the remnant of them the fire consumeth.
\vs{21}Acquaint now thyself with him, and be at peace: thereby good shall come unto thee.
\vs{22}Receive, I pray thee, the law from his mouth, and lay up his words in thine heart.
\vs{23}If thou return to the Almighty, thou shalt be built up, thou shalt put away iniquity far from thy tabernacles.
\vs{24}Then shalt thou lay up gold as dust, and the gold of Ophir as the stones of the brooks.
\vs{25}Yea, the Almighty shall be thy defence, and thou shalt have plenty of silver.
\vs{26}For then shalt thou have thy delight in the Almighty, and shalt lift up thy face unto God.
\vs{27}Thou shalt make thy prayer unto him, and he shall hear thee, and thou shalt pay thy vows.
\vs{28}Thou shalt also decree a thing, and it shall be established unto thee: and the light shall shine upon thy ways.

\vs{30}He shall deliver the island of the innocent: and it is delivered by the pureness of thine hands.

##### Chapter 23

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="23">
<p><span class="drop-cap">T</span>hen Job answered and said, <span class="verse-number">2</span> Even to day is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning. <span class="verse-number">3</span> Oh that I knew where I might find him! that I might come even to his seat! <span class="verse-number">4</span> I would order my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments. <span class="verse-number">5</span> I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me. <span class="verse-number">6</span> Will he plead against me with his great power? No; but he would put strength in me. <span class="verse-number">7</span> There the righteous might dispute with him; so should I be delivered for ever from my judge. <span class="verse-number">8</span> Behold, I go forward, but he is not there; and backward, but I cannot perceive him: <span class="verse-number">9</span> On the left hand, where he doth work, but I cannot behold him: he hideth himself on the right hand, that I cannot see him: <span class="verse-number">10</span> But he knoweth the way that I take: when he hath tried me, I shall come forth as gold. <span class="verse-number">11</span> My foot hath held his steps, his way have I kept, and not declined. <span class="verse-number">12</span> Neither have I gone back from the commandment of his lips; I have esteemed the words of his mouth more than my necessary food. <span class="verse-number">13</span> But he is in one mind, and who can turn him? and what his soul desireth, even that he doeth. <span class="verse-number">14</span> For he performeth the thing that is appointed for me: and many such things are with him. <span class="verse-number">15</span> Therefore am I troubled at his presence: when I consider, I am afraid of him. <span class="verse-number">16</span> For God maketh my heart soft, and the Almighty troubleth me: <span class="verse-number">17</span> Because I was not cut off before the darkness, neither hath he covered the darkness from my face.</p>
</div>
:::

##### Chapter 24

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="24">
<p><span class="drop-cap">W</span>hy, seeing times are not hidden from the Almighty, do they that know him not see his days? <span class="verse-number">2</span> Some remove the landmarks; they violently take away flocks, and feed thereof. <span class="verse-number">3</span> They drive away the ass of the fatherless, they take the widow's ox for a pledge. <span class="verse-number">4</span> They turn the needy out of the way: the poor of the earth hide themselves together. <span class="verse-number">5</span> Behold, as wild asses in the desert, go they forth to their work; rising betimes for a prey: the wilderness yieldeth food for them and for their children. <span class="verse-number">6</span> They reap every one his corn in the field: and they gather the vintage of the wicked. <span class="verse-number">7</span> They cause the naked to lodge without clothing, that they have no covering in the cold. <span class="verse-number">8</span> They are wet with the showers of the mountains, and embrace the rock for want of a shelter. <span class="verse-number">9</span> They pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge of the poor. <span class="verse-number">10</span> They cause him to go naked without clothing, and they take away the sheaf from the hungry; <span class="verse-number">11</span> Which make oil within their walls, and tread their winepresses, and suffer thirst. <span class="verse-number">12</span> Men groan from out of the city, and the soul of the wounded crieth out: yet God layeth not folly to them. <span class="verse-number">13</span> They are of those that rebel against the light; they know not the ways thereof, nor abide in the paths thereof. <span class="verse-number">14</span> The murderer rising with the light killeth the poor and needy, and in the night is as a thief. <span class="verse-number">15</span> The eye also of the adulterer waiteth for the twilight, saying, No eye shall see me: and disguiseth his face. <span class="verse-number">16</span> In the dark they dig through houses, which they had marked for themselves in the daytime: they know not the light. <span class="verse-number">17</span> For the morning is to them even as the shadow of death: if one know them, they are in the terrors of the shadow of death. <span class="verse-number">18</span> He is swift as the waters; their portion is cursed in the earth: he beholdeth not the way of the vineyards. <span class="verse-number">19</span> Drought and heat consume the snow waters: so doth the grave those which have sinned. <span class="verse-number">20</span> The womb shall forget him; the worm shall feed sweetly on him; he shall be no more remembered; and wickedness shall be broken as a tree. <span class="verse-number">21</span> He evil entreateth the barren that beareth not: and doeth not good to the widow. <span class="verse-number">22</span> He draweth also the mighty with his power: he riseth up, and no man is sure of life. <span class="verse-number">23</span> Though it be given him to be in safety, whereon he resteth; yet his eyes are upon their ways. <span class="verse-number">24</span> They are exalted for a little while, but are gone and brought low; they are taken out of the way as all other, and cut off as the tops of the ears of corn. <span class="verse-number">25</span> And if it be not so now, who will make me a liar, and make my speech nothing worth?</p>
</div>
:::

##### Chapter 26

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="26">
<p><span class="drop-cap">B</span>ut Job answered and said, <span class="verse-number">2</span> How hast thou helped him that is without power? how savest thou the arm that hath no strength? <span class="verse-number">3</span> How hast thou counselled him that hath no wisdom? and how hast thou plentifully declared the thing as it is? <span class="verse-number">4</span> To whom hast thou uttered words? and whose spirit came from thee? <span class="verse-number">5</span> Dead things are formed from under the waters, and the inhabitants thereof. <span class="verse-number">6</span> Hell is naked before him, and destruction hath no covering. <span class="verse-number">7</span> He stretcheth out the north over the empty place, and hangeth the earth upon nothing. <span class="verse-number">8</span> He bindeth up the waters in his thick clouds; and the cloud is not rent under them. <span class="verse-number">9</span> He holdeth back the face of his throne, and spreadeth his cloud upon it. <span class="verse-number">10</span> He hath compassed the waters with bounds, until the day and night come to an end. <span class="verse-number">11</span> The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at his reproof. <span class="verse-number">12</span> He divideth the sea with his power, and by his understanding he smiteth through the proud. <span class="verse-number">13</span> By his spirit he hath garnished the heavens; his hand hath formed the crooked serpent. <span class="verse-number">14</span> Lo, these are parts of his ways: but how little a portion is heard of him? but the thunder of his power who can understand?</p>
</div>
:::

##### Chapter 27

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="27">
<p><span class="drop-cap">M</span>oreover Job continued his parable, and said, <span class="verse-number">2</span> As God liveth, who hath taken away my judgment; and the Almighty, who hath vexed my soul; <span class="verse-number">3</span> All the while my breath is in me, and the spirit of God is in my nostrils; <span class="verse-number">4</span> My lips shall not speak wickedness, nor my tongue utter deceit. <span class="verse-number">5</span> God forbid that I should justify you: till I die I will not remove mine integrity from me. <span class="verse-number">6</span> My righteousness I hold fast, and will not let it go: my heart shall not reproach me so long as I live. <span class="verse-number">7</span> Let mine enemy be as the wicked, and he that riseth up against me as the unrighteous. <span class="verse-number">8</span> For what is the hope of the hypocrite, though he hath gained, when God taketh away his soul? <span class="verse-number">9</span> Will God hear his cry when trouble cometh upon him? <span class="verse-number">10</span> Will he delight himself in the Almighty? will he always call upon God? <span class="verse-number">11</span> I will teach you by the hand of God: that which is with the Almighty will I not conceal. <span class="verse-number">12</span> Behold, all ye yourselves have seen it; why then are ye thus altogether vain? <span class="verse-number">13</span> This is the portion of a wicked man with God, and the heritage of oppressors, which they shall receive of the Almighty. <span class="verse-number">14</span> If his children be multiplied, it is for the sword: and his offspring shall not be satisfied with bread. <span class="verse-number">15</span> Those that remain of him shall be buried in death: and his widows shall not weep. <span class="verse-number">16</span> Though he heap up silver as the dust, and prepare raiment as the clay; <span class="verse-number">17</span> He may prepare it, but the just shall put it on, and the innocent shall divide the silver. <span class="verse-number">18</span> He buildeth his house as a moth, and as a booth that the keeper maketh. <span class="verse-number">19</span> The rich man shall lie down, but he shall not be gathered: he openeth his eyes, and he is not. <span class="verse-number">20</span> Terrors take hold on him as waters, a tempest stealeth him away in the night. <span class="verse-number">21</span> The east wind carrieth him away, and he departeth: and as a storm hurleth him out of his place. <span class="verse-number">22</span> For God shall cast upon him, and not spare: he would fain flee out of his hand. <span class="verse-number">23</span> Men shall clap their hands at him, and shall hiss him out of his place.</p>
</div>

##### Chapter 28

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="28">
<p><span class="drop-cap">S</span>urely there is a vein for the silver, and a place for gold where they fine it. <span class="verse-number">2</span> Iron is taken out of the earth, and brass is molten out of the stone. <span class="verse-number">3</span> He setteth an end to darkness, and searcheth out all perfection: the stones of darkness, and the shadow of death. <span class="verse-number">4</span> The flood breaketh out from the inhabitant; even the waters forgotten of the foot: they are dried up, they are gone away from men. <span class="verse-number">5</span> As for the earth, out of it cometh bread: and under it is turned up as it were fire. <span class="verse-number">6</span> The stones of it are the place of sapphires: and it hath dust of gold. <span class="verse-number">7</span> There is a path which no fowl knoweth, and which the vulture's eye hath not seen: <span class="verse-number">8</span> The lion's whelps have not trodden it, nor the fierce lion passed by it. <span class="verse-number">9</span> He putteth forth his hand upon the rock; he overturneth the mountains by the roots. <span class="verse-number">10</span> He cutteth out rivers among the rocks; and his eye seeth every precious thing. <span class="verse-number">11</span> He bindeth the floods from overflowing; and the thing that is hid bringeth he forth to light. <span class="verse-number">12</span> But where shall wisdom be found? and where is the place of understanding? <span class="verse-number">13</span> Man knoweth not the price thereof; neither is it found in the land of the living. <span class="verse-number">14</span> The depth saith, It is not in me: and the sea saith, It is not with me. <span class="verse-number">15</span> It cannot be gotten for gold, neither shall silver be weighed for the price thereof. <span class="verse-number">16</span> It cannot be valued with the gold of Ophir, with the precious onyx, or the sapphire. <span class="verse-number">17</span> The gold and the crystal cannot equal it: and the exchange of it shall not be for jewels of fine gold. <span class="verse-number">18</span> No mention shall be made of coral, or of pearls: for the price of wisdom is above rubies. <span class="verse-number">19</span> The topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it, neither shall it be valued with pure gold. <span class="verse-number">20</span> Whence then cometh wisdom? and where is the place of understanding? <span class="verse-number">21</span> Seeing it is hid from the eyes of all living, and kept close from the fowls of the air. <span class="verse-number">22</span> Destruction and death say, We have heard the fame thereof with our ears. <span class="verse-number">23</span> God understandeth the way thereof, and he knoweth the place thereof. <span class="verse-number">24</span> For he looketh to the ends of the earth, and seeth under the whole heaven; <span class="verse-number">25</span> To make the weight for the winds; and he weigheth the waters by measure. <span class="verse-number">26</span> When he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunder: <span class="verse-number">27</span> Then did he see it, and declare it; he prepared it, yea, and searched it out. <span class="verse-number">28</span> And unto man he said, Behold, the fear of the LORD, that is wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding.</p>
</div>
:::

##### Chapter 29

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="29">
<p><span class="drop-cap">M</span>oreover Job continued his parable, and said, <span class="verse-number">2</span> Oh that I were as in months past, as in the days when God preserved me; <span class="verse-number">3</span> When his candle shined upon my head, and when by his light I walked through darkness; <span class="verse-number">4</span> As I was in the days of my youth, when the secret of God was upon my tabernacle; <span class="verse-number">5</span> When the Almighty was yet with me, when my children were about me; <span class="verse-number">6</span> When I washed my steps with butter, and the rock poured me out rivers of oil; <span class="verse-number">7</span> When I went out to the gate through the city, when I prepared my seat in the street! <span class="verse-number">8</span> The young men saw me, and hid themselves: and the aged arose, and stood up. <span class="verse-number">9</span> The princes refrained talking, and laid their hand on their mouth. <span class="verse-number">10</span> The nobles held their peace, and their tongue cleaved to the roof of their mouth. <span class="verse-number">11</span> When the ear heard me, then it blessed me; and when the eye saw me, it gave witness to me: <span class="verse-number">12</span> Because I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and him that had none to help him. <span class="verse-number">13</span> The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me: and I caused the widow's heart to sing for joy. <span class="verse-number">14</span> I put on righteousness, and it clothed me: my judgment was as a robe and a diadem. <span class="verse-number">15</span> I was eyes to the blind, and feet was I to the lame. <span class="verse-number">16</span> I was a father to the poor: and the cause which I knew not I searched out. <span class="verse-number">17</span> And I brake the jaws of the wicked, and plucked the spoil out of his teeth. <span class="verse-number">18</span> Then I said, I shall die in my nest, and I shall multiply my days as the sand. <span class="verse-number">19</span> My root was spread out by the waters, and the dew lay all night upon my branch. <span class="verse-number">20</span> My glory was fresh in me, and my bow was renewed in my hand. <span class="verse-number">21</span> Unto me men gave ear, and waited, and kept silence at my counsel. <span class="verse-number">22</span> After my words they spake not again; and my speech dropped upon them. <span class="verse-number">23</span> And they waited for me as for the rain; and they opened their mouth wide as for the latter rain. <span class="verse-number">24</span> If I laughed on them, they believed it not; and the light of my countenance they cast not down. <span class="verse-number">25</span> I chose out their way, and sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one that comforteth the mourners.</p>
</div>
:::

##### Chapter 30

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="30">
<p><span class="drop-cap">B</span>ut now they that are younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I would have disdained to have set with the dogs of my flock. <span class="verse-number">2</span> Yea, whereto might the strength of their hands profit me, in whom old age was perished? <span class="verse-number">3</span> For want and famine they were solitary; fleeing into the wilderness in former time desolate and waste. <span class="verse-number">4</span> Who cut up mallows by the bushes, and juniper roots for their meat. <span class="verse-number">5</span> They were driven forth from among men, (they cried after them as after a thief;) <span class="verse-number">6</span> To dwell in the cliffs of the valleys, in caves of the earth, and in the rocks. <span class="verse-number">7</span> Among the bushes they brayed; under the nettles they were gathered together. <span class="verse-number">8</span> They were children of fools, yea, children of base men: they were viler than the earth. <span class="verse-number">9</span> And now am I their song, yea, I am their byword. <span class="verse-number">10</span> They abhor me, they flee far from me, and spare not to spit in my face. <span class="verse-number">11</span> Because he hath loosed my cord, and afflicted me, they have also let loose the bridle before me. <span class="verse-number">12</span> Upon my right hand rise the youth; they push away my feet, and they raise up against me the ways of their destruction. <span class="verse-number">13</span> They mar my path, they set forward my calamity, they have no helper. <span class="verse-number">14</span> They came upon me as a wide breaking in of waters: in the desolation they rolled themselves upon me. <span class="verse-number">15</span> Terrors are turned upon me: they pursue my soul as the wind: and my welfare passeth away as a cloud. <span class="verse-number">16</span> And now my soul is poured out upon me; the days of affliction have taken hold upon me. <span class="verse-number">17</span> My bones are pierced in me in the night season: and my sinews take no rest. <span class="verse-number">18</span> By the great force of my disease is my garment changed: it bindeth me about as the collar of my coat. <span class="verse-number">19</span> He hath cast me into the mire, and I am become like dust and ashes. <span class="verse-number">20</span> I cry unto thee, and thou dost not hear me: I stand up, and thou regardest me not. <span class="verse-number">21</span> Thou art become cruel to me: with thy strong hand thou opposest thyself against me. <span class="verse-number">22</span> Thou liftest me up to the wind; thou causest me to ride upon it, and dissolvest my substance. <span class="verse-number">23</span> For I know that thou wilt bring me to death, and to the house appointed for all living. <span class="verse-number">24</span> Howbeit he will not stretch out his hand to the grave, though they cry in his destruction. <span class="verse-number">25</span> Did not I weep for him that was in trouble? was not my soul grieved for the poor? <span class="verse-number">26</span> When I looked for good, then evil came unto me: and when I waited for light, there came darkness. <span class="verse-number">27</span> My bowels boiled, and rested not: the days of affliction prevented me. <span class="verse-number">28</span> I went mourning without the sun: I stood up, and I cried in the congregation. <span class="verse-number">29</span> I am a brother to dragons, and a companion to owls. <span class="verse-number">30</span> My skin is black upon me, and my bones are burned with heat. <span class="verse-number">31</span> My harp also is turned to mourning, and my organ into the voice of them that weep.</p>
</div>
:::

##### Chapter 31

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="31">
<p><span class="drop-cap">I</span> made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid? <span class="verse-number">2</span> For what portion of God is there from above? and what inheritance of the Almighty from on high? <span class="verse-number">3</span> Is not destruction to the wicked? and a strange punishment to the workers of iniquity? <span class="verse-number">4</span> Doth not he see my ways, and count all my steps? <span class="verse-number">5</span> If I have walked with vanity, or if my foot hath hasted to deceit; <span class="verse-number">6</span> Let me be weighed in an even balance that God may know mine integrity. <span class="verse-number">7</span> If my step hath turned out of the way, and mine heart walked after mine eyes, and if any blot hath cleaved to mine hands; <span class="verse-number">8</span> Then let me sow, and let another eat; yea, let my offspring be rooted out. <span class="verse-number">9</span> If mine heart have been deceived by a woman, or if I have laid wait at my neighbour's door; <span class="verse-number">10</span> Then let my wife grind unto another, and let others bow down upon her. <span class="verse-number">11</span> For this is an heinous crime; yea, it is an iniquity to be punished by the judges. <span class="verse-number">12</span> For it is a fire that consumeth to destruction, and would root out all mine increase. <span class="verse-number">13</span> If I did despise the cause of my manservant or of my maidservant, when they contended with me; <span class="verse-number">14</span> What then shall I do when God riseth up? and when he visiteth, what shall I answer him? <span class="verse-number">15</span> Did not he that made me in the womb make him? and did not one fashion us in the womb? <span class="verse-number">16</span> If I have withheld the poor from their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail; <span class="verse-number">17</span> Or have eaten my morsel myself alone, and the fatherless hath not eaten thereof; <span class="verse-number">18</span> (For from my youth he was brought up with me, as with a father, and I have guided her from my mother's womb;) <span class="verse-number">19</span> If I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or any poor without covering; <span class="verse-number">20</span> If his loins have not blessed me, and if he were not warmed with the fleece of my sheep; <span class="verse-number">21</span> If I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, when I saw my help in the gate: <span class="verse-number">22</span> Then let mine arm fall from my shoulder blade, and mine arm be broken from the bone. <span class="verse-number">23</span> For destruction from God was a terror to me, and by reason of his highness I could not endure. <span class="verse-number">24</span> If I have made gold my hope, or have said to the fine gold, Thou art my confidence; <span class="verse-number">25</span> If I rejoice because my wealth was great, and because mine hand had gotten much; <span class="verse-number">26</span> If I beheld the sun when it shined, or the moon walking in brightness; <span class="verse-number">27</span> And my heart hath been secretly enticed, or my mouth hath kissed my hand: <span class="verse-number">28</span> This also were an iniquity to be punished by the judge: for I should have denied the God that is above. <span class="verse-number">29</span> If I rejoice at the destruction of him that hated me, or lifted up myself when evil found him: <span class="verse-number">30</span> Neither have I suffered my mouth to sin by wishing a curse to his soul. <span class="verse-number">31</span> If the men of my tabernacle said not, Oh that we had of his flesh! we cannot be satisfied. <span class="verse-number">32</span> The stranger did not lodge in the street: but I opened my doors to the traveller. <span class="verse-number">33</span> If I covered my transgressions as Adam, by hiding mine iniquity in my bosom: <span class="verse-number">34</span> Did I fear a great multitude, or did the contempt of families terrify me, that I kept silence, and went not out of the door? <span class="verse-number">35</span> Oh that one would hear me! behold, my desire is, that the Almighty would answer me, and that mine adversary had written a book. <span class="verse-number">36</span> Surely I would take it upon my shoulder, and bind it as a crown to me. <span class="verse-number">37</span> I would declare unto him the number of my steps; as a prince would I go near unto him. <span class="verse-number">38</span> If my land cry against me, or that the furrows likewise thereof complain; <span class="verse-number">39</span> If I have eaten the fruits thereof without money, or have caused the owners thereof to lose their life: <span class="verse-number">40</span> Let thistles grow instead of wheat, and cockle instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.</p>
</div>

\begin{scripture}[Job][31]
\lettrine[lines=4]{I}{} made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?
\vs{2}For what portion of God is there from above? and what inheritance of the Almighty from on high?
\vs{3}Is not destruction to the wicked? and a strange punishment to the workers of iniquity?
\vs{4}Doth not he see my ways, and count all my steps?
\vs{5}If I have walked with vanity, or if my foot hath hasted to deceit;
\vs{6}Let me be weighed in an even balance that God may know mine integrity.
\vs{7}If my step hath turned out of the way, and mine heart walked after mine eyes, and if any blot hath cleaved to mine hands;
\vs{8}Then let me sow, and let another eat; yea, let my offspring be rooted out.
\vs{9}If mine heart have been deceived by a woman, or if I have laid wait at my neighbour's door;
\vs{10}Then let my wife grind unto another, and let others bow down upon her.
\vs{11}For this is an heinous crime; yea, it is an iniquity to be punished by the judges.
\vs{12}For it is a fire that consumeth to destruction, and would root out all mine increase.
\vs{13}If I did despise the cause of my manservant or of my maidservant, when they contended with me;
\vs{14}What then shall I do when God riseth up? and when he visiteth, what shall I answer him?
\vs{15}Did not he that made me in the womb make him? and did not one fashion us in the womb?
\vs{16}If I have withheld the poor from their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail;
\vs{17}Or have eaten my morsel myself alone, and the fatherless hath not eaten thereof;
\vs{18}(For from my youth he was brought up with me, as with a father, and I have guided her from my mother's womb;)
\vs{19}If I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or any poor without covering;
\vs{20}If his loins have not blessed me, and if he were not warmed with the fleece of my sheep;
\vs{21}If I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, when I saw my help in the gate:
\vs{22}Then let mine arm fall from my shoulder blade, and mine arm be broken from the bone.
\vs{23}For destruction from God was a terror to me, and by reason of his highness I could not endure.
\vs{24}If I have made gold my hope, or have said to the fine gold, Thou art my confidence;
\vs{25}If I rejoice because my wealth was great, and because mine hand had gotten much;
\vs{26}If I beheld the sun when it shined, or the moon walking in brightness;
\vs{27}And my heart hath been secretly enticed, or my mouth hath kissed my hand:
\vs{28}This also were an iniquity to be punished by the judge: for I should have denied the God that is above.
\vs{29}If I rejoice at the destruction of him that hated me, or lifted up myself when evil found him:
\vs{30}Neither have I suffered my mouth to sin by wishing a curse to his soul.
\vs{31}If the men of my tabernacle said not, Oh that we had of his flesh! we cannot be satisfied.
\vs{32}The stranger did not lodge in the street: but I opened my doors to the traveller.
\vs{33}If I covered my transgressions as Adam, by hiding mine iniquity in my bosom:
\vs{34}Did I fear a great multitude, or did the contempt of families terrify me, that I kept silence, and went not out of the door?
\vs{35}Oh that one would hear me! behold, my desire is, that the Almighty would answer me, and that mine adversary had written a book.
\vs{36}Surely I would take it upon my shoulder, and bind it as a crown to me.
\vs{37}I would declare unto him the number of my steps; as a prince would I go near unto him.
\vs{38}If my land cry against me, or that the furrows likewise thereof complain;
\vs{39}If I have eaten the fruits thereof without money, or have caused the owners thereof to lose their life:
\vs{40}Let thistles grow instead of wheat, and cockle instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.
\end{scripture}

##### Chapter 32

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="32">
<p><span class="drop-cap">S</span>o these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes. <span class="verse-number">2</span> Then was kindled the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the kindred of Ram: against Job was his wrath kindled, because he justified himself rather than God. <span class="verse-number">3</span> Also against his three friends was his wrath kindled, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job. <span class="verse-number">4</span> Now Elihu had waited till Job had spoken, because they were elder than he. <span class="verse-number">5</span> When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, then his wrath was kindled. <span class="verse-number">6</span> And Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, I am young, and ye are very old; wherefore I was afraid, and durst not shew you mine opinion. <span class="verse-number">7</span> I said, Days should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom. <span class="verse-number">8</span> But there is a spirit in man: and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding. <span class="verse-number">9</span> Great men are not always wise: neither do the aged understand judgment. <span class="verse-number">10</span> Therefore I said, Hearken to me; I also will shew mine opinion. <span class="verse-number">11</span> Behold, I waited for your words; I gave ear to your reasons, whilst ye searched out what to say. <span class="verse-number">12</span> Yea, I attended unto you, and, behold, there was none of you that convinced Job, or that answered his words: <span class="verse-number">13</span> Lest ye should say, We have found out wisdom: God thrusteth him down, not man. <span class="verse-number">14</span> Now he hath not directed his words against me: neither will I answer him with your speeches. <span class="verse-number">15</span> They were amazed, they answered no more: they left off speaking. <span class="verse-number">16</span> When I had waited, (for they spake not, but stood still, and answered no more;) <span class="verse-number">17</span> I said, I will answer also my part, I also will shew mine opinion. <span class="verse-number">18</span> For I am full of matter, the spirit within me constraineth me. <span class="verse-number">19</span> Behold, my belly is as wine which hath no vent; it is ready to burst like new bottles. <span class="verse-number">20</span> I will speak, that I may be refreshed: I will open my lips and answer. <span class="verse-number">21</span> Let me not, I pray you, accept any man's person, neither let me give flattering titles unto man. <span class="verse-number">22</span> For I know not to give flattering titles; in so doing my maker would soon take me away.</p>
</div>
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
\begin{scripture}[Job][32]
\lettrine[lines=4]{S}{o} these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
\vs{2}Then was kindled the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the kindred of Ram: against Job was his wrath kindled, because he justified himself rather than God.
\vs{3}Also against his three friends was his wrath kindled, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.
\vs{4}Now Elihu had waited till Job had spoken, because they were elder than he.
\vs{5}When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, then his wrath was kindled.
\vs{6}And Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, I am young, and ye are very old; wherefore I was afraid, and durst not shew you mine opinion.
\vs{7}I said, Days should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom.
\vs{8}But there is a spirit in man: and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding.
\vs{9}Great men are not always wise: neither do the aged understand judgment.
\vs{10}Therefore I said, Hearken to me; I also will shew mine opinion.
\vs{11}Behold, I waited for your words; I gave ear to your reasons, whilst ye searched out what to say.
\vs{12}Yea, I attended unto you, and, behold, there was none of you that convinced Job, or that answered his words:
\vs{13}Lest ye should say, We have found out wisdom: God thrusteth him down, not man.
\vs{14}Now he hath not directed his words against me: neither will I answer him with your speeches.
\vs{15}They were amazed, they answered no more: they left off speaking.
\vs{16}When I had waited, (for they spake not, but stood still, and answered no more;)
\vs{17}I said, I will answer also my part, I also will shew mine opinion.
\vs{18}For I am full of matter, the spirit within me constraineth me.
\vs{19}Behold, my belly is as wine which hath no vent; it is ready to burst like new bottles.
\vs{20}I will speak, that I may be refreshed: I will open my lips and answer.
\vs{21}Let me not, I pray you, accept any man's person, neither let me give flattering titles unto man.
\vs{22}For I know not to give flattering titles; in so doing my maker would soon take me away.

##### Chapter 33

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="33">
<p><span class="drop-cap">W</span>herefore, Job, I pray thee, hear my speeches, and hearken to all my words. <span class="verse-number">2</span> Behold, now I have opened my mouth, my tongue hath spoken in my mouth. <span class="verse-number">3</span> My words shall be of the uprightness of my heart: and my lips shall utter knowledge clearly. <span class="verse-number">4</span> The spirit of God hath made me, and the breath of the Almighty hath given me life. <span class="verse-number">5</span> If thou canst answer me, set thy words in order before me, stand up. <span class="verse-number">6</span> Behold, I am according to thy wish in God's stead: I also am formed out of the clay. <span class="verse-number">7</span> Behold, my terror shall not make thee afraid, neither shall my hand be heavy upon thee. <span class="verse-number">8</span> Surely thou hast spoken in mine hearing, and I have heard the voice of thy words, saying, <span class="verse-number">9</span> I am clean without transgression, I am innocent; neither is there iniquity in me. <span class="verse-number">10</span> Behold, he findeth occasions against me, he counteth me for his enemy, <span class="verse-number">11</span> He putteth my feet in the stocks, he marketh all my paths. <span class="verse-number">12</span> Behold, in this thou art not just: I will answer thee, that God is greater than man. <span class="verse-number">13</span> Why dost thou strive against him? for he giveth not account of any of his matters. <span class="verse-number">14</span> For God speaketh once, yea twice, yet man perceiveth it not. <span class="verse-number">15</span> In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falleth upon men, in slumberings upon the bed; <span class="verse-number">16</span> Then he openeth the ears of men, and sealeth their instruction, <span class="verse-number">17</span> That he may withdraw man from his purpose, and hide pride from man. <span class="verse-number">18</span> He keepeth back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword. <span class="verse-number">19</span> He is chastened also with pain upon his bed, and the multitude of his bones with strong pain: <span class="verse-number">20</span> So that his life abhorreth bread, and his soul dainty meat. <span class="verse-number">21</span> His flesh is consumed away, that it cannot be seen; and his bones that were not seen stick out. <span class="verse-number">22</span> Yea, his soul draweth near unto the grave, and his life to the destroyers. <span class="verse-number">23</span> If there be a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to shew unto man his uprightness: <span class="verse-number">24</span> Then he is gracious unto him, and saith, Deliver him from going down to the pit: I have found a ransom. <span class="verse-number">25</span> His flesh shall be fresher than a child's: he shall return to the days of his youth: <span class="verse-number">26</span> He shall pray unto God, and he will be favourable unto him: and he shall see his face with joy: for he will render unto man his righteousness. <span class="verse-number">27</span> He looketh upon men, and if any say, I have sinned, and perverted that which was right, and it profited me not; <span class="verse-number">28</span> He will deliver his soul from going into the pit, and his life shall see the light. <span class="verse-number">29</span> Lo, all these things worketh God oftentimes with man, <span class="verse-number">30</span> To bring back his soul from the pit, to be enlightened with the light of the living. <span class="verse-number">31</span> Mark well, O Job, hearken unto me: hold thy peace, and I will speak. <span class="verse-number">32</span> If thou hast anything to say, answer me: speak, for I desire to justify thee. <span class="verse-number">33</span> If not, hearken unto me: hold thy peace, and I shall teach thee wisdom.</p>
</div>
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
\begin{scripture}[Job][33]
\lettrine[lines=4]{W}{herefore,} Job, I pray thee, hear my speeches, and hearken to all my words.
\vs{2}Behold, now I have opened my mouth, my tongue hath spoken in my mouth.
\vs{3}My words shall be of the uprightness of my heart: and my lips shall utter knowledge clearly.
\vs{4}The spirit of God hath made me, and the breath of the Almighty hath given me life.
\vs{5}If thou canst answer me, set thy words in order before me, stand up.
\vs{6}Behold, I am according to thy wish in God's stead: I also am formed out of the clay.
\vs{7}Behold, my terror shall not make thee afraid, neither shall my hand be heavy upon thee.
\vs{8}Surely thou hast spoken in mine hearing, and I have heard the voice of thy words, saying,
\vs{9}I am clean without transgression, I am innocent; neither is there iniquity in me.
\vs{10}Behold, he findeth occasions against me, he counteth me for his enemy,
\vs{11}He putteth my feet in the stocks, he marketh all my paths.
\vs{12}Behold, in this thou art not just: I will answer thee, that God is greater than man.
\vs{13}Why dost thou strive against him? for he giveth not account of any of his matters.
\vs{14}For God speaketh once, yea twice, yet man perceiveth it not.
\vs{15}In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falleth upon men, in slumberings upon the bed;
\vs{16}Then he openeth the ears of men, and sealeth their instruction,
\vs{17}That he may withdraw man from his purpose, and hide pride from man.
\vs{18}He keepeth back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword.
\vs{19}He is chastened also with pain upon his bed, and the multitude of his bones with strong pain:
\vs{20}So that his life abhorreth bread, and his soul dainty meat.
\vs{21}His flesh is consumed away, that it cannot be seen; and his bones that were not seen stick out.
\vs{22}Yea, his soul draweth near unto the grave, and his life to the destroyers.
\vs{23}If there be a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to shew unto man his uprightness:
\vs{24}Then he is gracious unto him, and saith, Deliver him from going down to the pit: I have found a ransom.
\vs{25}His flesh shall be fresher than a child's: he shall return to the days of his youth:
\vs{26}He shall pray unto God, and he will be favourable unto him: and he shall see his face with joy: for he will render unto man his righteousness.
\vs{27}He looketh upon men, and if any say, I have sinned, and perverted that which was right, and it profited me not;
\vs{28}He will deliver his soul from going into the pit, and his life shall see the light.
\vs{29}Lo, all these things worketh God oftentimes with man,
\vs{30}To bring back his soul from the pit, to be enlightened with the light of the living.
\vs{31}Mark well, O Job, hearken unto me: hold thy peace, and I will speak.
\vs{32}If thou hast anything to say, answer me: speak, for I desire to justify thee.
\vs{33}If not, hearken unto me: hold thy peace, and I shall teach thee wisdom.
\end{scripture}

##### Chapter 34

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="34">
<p><span class="drop-cap">F</span>urthermore Elihu answered and said, <span class="verse-number">2</span> Hear my words, O ye wise men; and give ear unto me, ye that have knowledge. <span class="verse-number">3</span> For the ear trieth words, as the mouth tasteth meat. <span class="verse-number">4</span> Let us choose to us judgment: let us know among ourselves what is good. <span class="verse-number">5</span> For Job hath said, I am righteous: and God hath taken away my judgment. <span class="verse-number">6</span> Should I lie against my right? my wound is incurable without transgression. <span class="verse-number">7</span> What man is like Job, who drinketh up scorning like water? <span class="verse-number">8</span> Which goeth in company with the workers of iniquity, and walketh with wicked men. <span class="verse-number">9</span> For he hath said, It profiteth a man nothing that he should delight himself with God. <span class="verse-number">10</span> Therefore hearken unto me ye men of understanding: far be it from God, that he should do wickedness; and from the Almighty, that he should commit iniquity. <span class="verse-number">11</span> For the work of a man shall he render unto him, and cause every man to find according to his ways. <span class="verse-number">12</span> Yea, surely God will not do wickedly, neither will the Almighty pervert judgment. <span class="verse-number">13</span> Who hath given him a charge over the earth? or who hath disposed the whole world? <span class="verse-number">14</span> If he set his heart upon man, if he gather unto himself his spirit and his breath; <span class="verse-number">15</span> All flesh shall perish together, and man shall turn again unto dust. <span class="verse-number">16</span> If now thou hast understanding, hear this: hearken to the voice of my words. <span class="verse-number">17</span> Shall even he that hateth right govern? and wilt thou condemn him that is most just? <span class="verse-number">18</span> Is it fit to say to a king, Thou art wicked? and to princes, Ye are ungodly? <span class="verse-number">19</span> How much less to him that accepteth not the persons of princes, nor regardeth the rich more than the poor? for they all are the work of his hands. <span class="verse-number">20</span> In a moment shall they die, and the people shall be troubled at midnight, and pass away: and the mighty shall be taken away without hand. <span class="verse-number">21</span> For his eyes are upon the ways of man, and he seeth all his goings. <span class="verse-number">22</span> There is no darkness, nor shadow of death, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves. <span class="verse-number">23</span> For he will not lay upon man more than right; that he should enter into judgment with God. <span class="verse-number">24</span> He shall break in pieces mighty men without number, and set others in their stead. <span class="verse-number">25</span> Therefore he knoweth their works, and he overturneth them in the night, so that they are destroyed. <span class="verse-number">26</span> He striketh them as wicked men in the open sight of others; <span class="verse-number">27</span> Because they turned back from him, and would not consider any of his ways: <span class="verse-number">28</span> So that they cause the cry of the poor to come unto him, and he heareth the cry of the afflicted. <span class="verse-number">29</span> When he giveth quietness, who then can make trouble? and when he hideth his face, who then can behold him? whether it be done against a nation, or against a man only: <span class="verse-number">30</span> That the hypocrite reign not, lest the people be ensnared. <span class="verse-number">31</span> Surely it is meet to be said unto God, I have borne chastisement, I will not offend any more: <span class="verse-number">32</span> That which I see not teach thou me: if I have done iniquity, I will do no more. <span class="verse-number">33</span> Should it be according to thy mind? he will recompense it, whether thou refuse, or whether thou choose; and not I: therefore speak what thou knowest. <span class="verse-number">34</span> Let men of understanding tell me, and let a wise man hearken unto me. <span class="verse-number">35</span> Job hath spoken without knowledge, and his words were without wisdom. <span class="verse-number">36</span> My desire is that Job may be tried unto the end because of his answers for wicked men. <span class="verse-number">37</span> For he addeth rebellion unto his sin, he clappeth his hands among us, and multiplieth his words against God.</p>
</div>
:::

\begin{scripture}[Job][34]

\vs{2}Hear my words, O ye wise men; and give ear unto me, ye that have knowledge.
\vs{3}For the ear trieth words, as the mouth tasteth meat.

\vs{35}Job hath spoken without knowledge, and his words were without wisdom.
\vs{36}My desire is that Job may be tried unto the end because of his answers for wicked men.
\vs{37}For he addeth rebellion unto his sin, he clappeth his hands among us, and multiplieth his words against God.
\end{scripture}
:::


##### Chapter 35

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="35">
<p><span class="drop-cap">E</span>lihu spake moreover, and said, <span class="verse-number">2</span> Thinkest thou this to be right, that thou saidst, My righteousness is more than God's? <span class="verse-number">3</span> For thou saidst, What advantage will it be unto thee? and, What profit shall I have, if I be cleansed from my sin? <span class="verse-number">4</span> I will answer thee, and thy companions with thee. <span class="verse-number">5</span> Look unto the heavens, and see; and behold the clouds which are higher than thou. <span class="verse-number">6</span> If thou sinnest, what doest thou against him? or if thy transgressions be multiplied, what doest thou unto him? <span class="verse-number">7</span> If thou be righteous, what givest thou him? or what receiveth he of thine hand? <span class="verse-number">8</span> Thy wickedness may hurt a man as thou art; and thy righteousness may profit the son of man. <span class="verse-number">9</span> By reason of the multitude of oppressions they make the oppressed to cry: they cry out by reason of the arm of the mighty. <span class="verse-number">10</span> But none saith, Where is God my maker, who giveth songs in the night; <span class="verse-number">11</span> Who teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth, and maketh us wiser than the fowls of heaven? <span class="verse-number">12</span> There they cry, but none giveth answer, because of the pride of evil men. <span class="verse-number">13</span> Surely God will not hear vanity, neither will the Almighty regard it. <span class="verse-number">14</span> Although thou sayest thou shalt not see him, yet judgment is before him; therefore trust thou in him. <span class="verse-number">15</span> But now, because it is not so, he hath visited in his anger; yet he knoweth it not in great extremity: <span class="verse-number">16</span> Therefore doth Job open his mouth in vain; he multiplieth words without knowledge.</p>
</div>
:::

##### Chapter 36

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="36">
<p><span class="drop-cap">E</span>lihu also proceeded, and said, <span class="verse-number">2</span> Suffer me a little, and I will shew thee that I have yet to speak on God's behalf. <span class="verse-number">3</span> I will fetch my knowledge from afar, and will ascribe righteousness to my Maker. <span class="verse-number">4</span> For truly my words shall not be false: he that is perfect in knowledge is with thee. <span class="verse-number">5</span> Behold, God is mighty, and despiseth not any: he is mighty in strength and wisdom. <span class="verse-number">6</span> He preserveth not the life of the wicked: but giveth right to the poor. <span class="verse-number">7</span> He withdraweth not his eyes from the righteous: but with kings are they on the throne; yea, he doth establish them for ever, and they are exalted. <span class="verse-number">8</span> And if they be bound in fetters, and be holden in cords of affliction; <span class="verse-number">9</span> Then he sheweth them their work, and their transgressions that they have exceeded. <span class="verse-number">10</span> He openeth also their ear to discipline, and commandeth that they return from iniquity. <span class="verse-number">11</span> If they obey and serve him, they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures. <span class="verse-number">12</span> But if they obey not, they shall perish by the sword, and they shall die without knowledge. <span class="verse-number">13</span> But the hypocrites in heart heap up wrath: they cry not when he bindeth them. <span class="verse-number">14</span> They die in youth, and their life is among the unclean. <span class="verse-number">15</span> He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression. <span class="verse-number">16</span> Even so would he have removed thee out of the strait into a broad place, where there is no straitness; and that which should be set on thy table should be full of fatness. <span class="verse-number">17</span> But thou hast fulfilled the judgment of the wicked: judgment and justice take hold on thee. <span class="verse-number">18</span> Because there is wrath, beware lest he take thee away with his stroke: then a great ransom cannot deliver thee. <span class="verse-number">19</span> Will he esteem thy riches? no, not gold, nor all the forces of strength. <span class="verse-number">20</span> Desire not the night, when people are cut off in their place. <span class="verse-number">21</span> Take heed, regard not iniquity: for this hast thou chosen rather than affliction. <span class="verse-number">22</span> Behold, God exalteth by his power: who teacheth like him? <span class="verse-number">23</span> Who hath enjoined him his way? or who can say, Thou hast wrought iniquity? <span class="verse-number">24</span> Remember that thou magnify his work, which men behold. <span class="verse-number">25</span> Every man may see it; man may behold it afar off. <span class="verse-number">26</span> Behold, God is great, and we know him not, neither can the number of his years be searched out. <span class="verse-number">27</span> For he maketh small the drops of water: they pour down rain according to the vapour thereof: <span class="verse-number">28</span> Which the clouds do drop and distil upon man abundantly. <span class="verse-number">29</span> Also can any understand the spreadings of the clouds, or the noise of his tabernacle? <span class="verse-number">30</span> Behold, he spreadeth his light upon it, and covereth the bottom of the sea. <span class="verse-number">31</span> For by them judgeth he the people; he giveth meat in abundance. <span class="verse-number">32</span> With clouds he covereth the light; and commandeth it not to shine by the cloud that cometh betwixt. <span class="verse-number">33</span> The noise thereof sheweth concerning it, the cattle also concerning the vapour.</p>
</div>
:::

\vs{5}Behold, God is mighty, and despiseth not any: he is mighty in strength and wisdom.
\vs{6}He preserveth not the life of the wicked: but giveth right to the poor.

\vs{8}And if they be bound in fetters, and be holden in cords of affliction;
\vs{9}Then he sheweth them their work, and their transgressions that they have exceeded.
\vs{10}He openeth also their ear to discipline, and commandeth that they return from iniquity.
\vs{11}If they obey and serve him, they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.
\vs{12}But if they obey not, they shall perish by the sword, and they shall die without knowledge.
\vs{13}But the hypocrites in heart heap up wrath: they cry not when he bindeth them.
\vs{14}They die in youth, and their life is among the unclean.
\vs{15}He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression.
\vs{16}Even so would he have removed thee out of the strait into a broad place, where there is no straitness; and that which should be set on thy table should be full of fatness.
\vs{17}But thou hast fulfilled the judgment of the wicked: judgment and justice take hold on thee.
\vs{18}Because there is wrath, beware lest he take thee away with his stroke: then a great ransom cannot deliver thee.
\vs{19}Will he esteem thy riches? no, not gold, nor all the forces of strength.
\vs{20}Desire not the night, when people are cut off in their place.
\vs{21}Take heed, regard not iniquity: for this hast thou chosen rather than affliction.
\vs{22}Behold, God exalteth by his power: who teacheth like him?
\vs{23}Who hath enjoined him his way? or who can say, Thou hast wrought iniquity?
\vs{24}Remember that thou magnify his work, which men behold.
\vs{25}Every man may see it; man may behold it afar off.
\vs{26}Behold, God is great, and we know him not, neither can the number of his years be searched out.
\vs{27}For he maketh small the drops of water: they pour down rain according to the vapour thereof:
\vs{28}Which the clouds do drop and distil upon man abundantly.
\vs{29}Also can any understand the spreadings of the clouds, or the noise of his tabernacle?
\vs{30}Behold, he spreadeth his light upon it, and covereth the bottom of the sea.
\vs{31}For by them judgeth he the people; he giveth meat in abundance.
\vs{32}With clouds he covereth the light; and commandeth it not to shine by the cloud that cometh betwixt.
\vs{33}The noise thereof sheweth concerning it, the cattle also concerning the vapour.
