##### Chapter 37

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="37">
<p><span class="drop-cap">A</span>t this also my heart trembleth, and is moved out of his place. <span class="verse-number">2</span> Hear attentively the noise of his voice, and the sound that goeth out of his mouth. <span class="verse-number">3</span> He directeth it under the whole heaven, and his lightning unto the ends of the earth. <span class="verse-number">4</span> After it a voice roareth: he thundereth with the voice of his excellency; and he will not stay them when his voice is heard. <span class="verse-number">5</span> God thundereth marvellously with his voice; great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend. <span class="verse-number">6</span> For he saith to the snow, Be thou on the earth; likewise to the small rain, and to the great rain of his strength. <span class="verse-number">7</span> He sealeth up the hand of every man; that all men may know his work. <span class="verse-number">8</span> Then the beasts go into dens, and remain in their places. <span class="verse-number">9</span> Out of the south cometh the whirlwind: and cold out of the north. <span class="verse-number">10</span> By the breath of God frost is given: and the breadth of the waters is straitened. <span class="verse-number">11</span> Also by watering he wearieth the thick cloud: he scattereth his bright cloud: <span class="verse-number">12</span> And it is turned round about by his counsels: that they may do whatsoever he commandeth them upon the face of the world in the earth. <span class="verse-number">13</span> He causeth it to come, whether for correction, or for his land, or for mercy. <span class="verse-number">14</span> Hearken unto this, O Job: stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God. <span class="verse-number">15</span> Dost thou know when God disposed them, and caused the light of his cloud to shine? <span class="verse-number">16</span> Dost thou know the balancings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him which is perfect in knowledge? <span class="verse-number">17</span> How thy garments are warm, when he quieteth the earth by the south wind? <span class="verse-number">18</span> Hast thou with him spread out the sky, which is strong, and as a molten looking glass? <span class="verse-number">19</span> Teach us what we shall say unto him; for we cannot order our speech by reason of darkness. <span class="verse-number">20</span> Shall it be told him that I speak? if a man speak, surely he shall be swallowed up. <span class="verse-number">21</span> And now men see not the bright light which is in the clouds: but the wind passeth, and cleanseth them. <span class="verse-number">22</span> Fair weather cometh out of the north: with God is terrible majesty. <span class="verse-number">23</span> Touching the Almighty, we cannot find him out: he is excellent in power, and in judgment, and in plenty of justice: he will not afflict. <span class="verse-number">24</span> Men do therefore fear him: he respecteth not any that are wise of heart.</p>
</div>
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}

##### Chapter 38

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="38">
<p><span class="drop-cap">T</span>hen the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said, <span class="verse-number">2</span> Who is this that darkeneth counsel by words without knowledge? <span class="verse-number">3</span> Gird up now thy loins like a man; for I will demand of thee, and answer thou me. <span class="verse-number">4</span> Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding. <span class="verse-number">5</span> Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest? or who hath stretched the line upon it? <span class="verse-number">6</span> Whereupon are the foundations thereof fastened? or who laid the corner stone thereof; <span class="verse-number">7</span> When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy? <span class="verse-number">8</span> Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it brake forth, as if it had issued out of the womb? <span class="verse-number">9</span> When I made the cloud the garment thereof, and thick darkness a swaddlingband for it, <span class="verse-number">10</span> And brake up for it my decreed place, and set bars and doors, <span class="verse-number">11</span> And said, Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further: and here shall thy proud waves be stayed? <span class="verse-number">12</span> Hast thou commanded the morning since thy days; and caused the dayspring to know his place; <span class="verse-number">13</span> That it might take hold of the ends of the earth, that the wicked might be shaken out of it? <span class="verse-number">14</span> It is turned as clay to the seal; and they stand as a garment. <span class="verse-number">15</span> And from the wicked their light is withholden, and the high arm shall be broken. <span class="verse-number">16</span> Hast thou entered into the springs of the sea? or hast thou walked in the search of the depth? <span class="verse-number">17</span> Have the gates of death been opened unto thee? or hast thou seen the doors of the shadow of death? <span class="verse-number">18</span> Hast thou perceived the breadth of the earth? declare if thou knowest it all. <span class="verse-number">19</span> Where is the way where light dwelleth? and as for darkness, where is the place thereof, <span class="verse-number">20</span> That thou shouldest take it to the bound thereof, and that thou shouldest know the paths to the house thereof? <span class="verse-number">21</span> Knowest thou it, because thou wast then born? or because the number of thy days is great? <span class="verse-number">22</span> Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow? or hast thou seen the treasures of the hail, <span class="verse-number">23</span> Which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war? <span class="verse-number">24</span> By what way is the light parted, which scattereth the east wind upon the earth? <span class="verse-number">25</span> Who hath divided a watercourse for the overflowing of waters, or a way for the lightning of thunder; <span class="verse-number">26</span> To cause it to rain on the earth, where no man is; on the wilderness, wherein there is no man; <span class="verse-number">27</span> To satisfy the desolate and waste ground; and to cause the bud of the tender herb to spring forth? <span class="verse-number">28</span> Hath the rain a father? or who hath begotten the drops of dew? <span class="verse-number">29</span> Out of whose womb came the ice? and the hoary frost of heaven, who hath gendered it? <span class="verse-number">30</span> The waters are hid as with a stone, and the face of the deep is frozen. <span class="verse-number">31</span> Canst thou bind the sweet influences of Pleiades, or loose the bands of Orion? <span class="verse-number">32</span> Canst thou bring forth Mazzaroth in his season? or canst thou guide Arcturus with his sons? <span class="verse-number">33</span> Knowest thou the ordinances of heaven? canst thou set the dominion thereof in the earth? <span class="verse-number">34</span> Canst thou lift up thy voice to the clouds, that abundance of waters may cover thee? <span class="verse-number">35</span> Canst thou send lightnings, that they may go and say unto thee, Here we are? <span class="verse-number">36</span> Who hath put wisdom in the inward parts? or who hath given understanding to the heart? <span class="verse-number">37</span> Who can number the clouds in wisdom? or who can stay the bottles of heaven, <span class="verse-number">38</span> When the dust groweth into hardness, and the clods cleave fast together? <span class="verse-number">39</span> Wilt thou hunt the prey for the lion? or fill the appetite of the young lions, <span class="verse-number">40</span> When they couch in their dens, and abide in the covert to lie in wait? <span class="verse-number">41</span> Who provideth for the raven his food? when his young ones cry unto God, they wander for lack of meat.</p>
</div>
:::

\begin{scripture}[Job][38]
\lettrine[lines=4]{T}{hen} the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said,
\vs{2}Who is this that darkeneth counsel by words without knowledge?
\vs{3}Gird up now thy loins like a man; for I will demand of thee, and answer thou me.
\vs{4}Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding.
\vs{5}Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest? or who hath stretched the line upon it?
\vs{6}Whereupon are the foundations thereof fastened? or who laid the corner stone thereof;
\vs{7}When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
\vs{8}Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it brake forth, as if it had issued out of the womb?
\vs{9}When I made the cloud the garment thereof, and thick darkness a swaddlingband for it,
\vs{10}And brake up for it my decreed place, and set bars and doors,
\vs{11}And said, Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further: and here shall thy proud waves be stayed?
\vs{12}Hast thou commanded the morning since thy days; and caused the dayspring to know his place;
\vs{13}That it might take hold of the ends of the earth, that the wicked might be shaken out of it?
\vs{14}It is turned as clay to the seal; and they stand as a garment.
\vs{15}And from the wicked their light is withholden, and the high arm shall be broken.
\vs{16}Hast thou entered into the springs of the sea? or hast thou walked in the search of the depth?
\vs{17}Have the gates of death been opened unto thee? or hast thou seen the doors of the shadow of death?
\vs{18}Hast thou perceived the breadth of the earth? declare if thou knowest it all.
\vs{19}Where is the way where light dwelleth? and as for darkness, where is the place thereof,
\vs{20}That thou shouldest take it to the bound thereof, and that thou shouldest know the paths to the house thereof?
\vs{21}Knowest thou it, because thou wast then born? or because the number of thy days is great?
\vs{22}Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow? or hast thou seen the treasures of the hail,
\vs{23}Which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war?
\vs{24}By what way is the light parted, which scattereth the east wind upon the earth?
\vs{25}Who hath divided a watercourse for the overflowing of waters, or a way for the lightning of thunder;
\vs{26}To cause it to rain on the earth, where no man is; on the wilderness, wherein there is no man;
\vs{27}To satisfy the desolate and waste ground; and to cause the bud of the tender herb to spring forth?
\vs{28}Hath the rain a father? or who hath begotten the drops of dew?
\vs{29}Out of whose womb came the ice? and the hoary frost of heaven, who hath gendered it?
\vs{30}The waters are hid as with a stone, and the face of the deep is frozen.
\vs{31}Canst thou bind the sweet influences of Pleiades, or loose the bands of Orion?
\vs{32}Canst thou bring forth Mazzaroth in his season? or canst thou guide Arcturus with his sons?
\vs{33}Knowest thou the ordinances of heaven? canst thou set the dominion thereof in the earth?
\vs{34}Canst thou lift up thy voice to the clouds, that abundance of waters may cover thee?
\vs{35}Canst thou send lightnings, that they may go and say unto thee, Here we are?
\vs{36}Who hath put wisdom in the inward parts? or who hath given understanding to the heart?
\vs{37}Who can number the clouds in wisdom? or who can stay the bottles of heaven,
\vs{38}When the dust groweth into hardness, and the clods cleave fast together?
\vs{39}Wilt thou hunt the prey for the lion? or fill the appetite of the young lions,
\vs{40}When they couch in their dens, and abide in the covert to lie in wait?
\vs{41}Who provideth for the raven his food? when his young ones cry unto God, they wander for lack of meat.
\end{scripture}

##### Chapter 39

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="39">
<p><span class="drop-cap">K</span>nowest thou the time when the wild goats of the rock bring forth? or canst thou mark when the hinds do calve? <span class="verse-number">2</span> Canst thou number the months that they fulfil? or knowest thou the time when they bring forth? <span class="verse-number">3</span> They bow themselves, they bring forth their young ones, they cast out their sorrows. <span class="verse-number">4</span> Their young ones are in good liking, they grow up with corn; they go forth, and return not unto them. <span class="verse-number">5</span> Who hath sent out the wild ass free? or who hath loosed the bands of the wild ass? <span class="verse-number">6</span> Whose house I have made the wilderness, and the barren land his dwellings. <span class="verse-number">7</span> He scorneth the multitude of the city, neither regardeth he the crying of the driver. <span class="verse-number">8</span> The range of the mountains is his pasture, and he searcheth after every green thing. <span class="verse-number">9</span> Will the unicorn be willing to serve thee, or abide by thy crib? <span class="verse-number">10</span> Canst thou bind the unicorn with his band in the furrow? or will he harrow the valleys after thee? <span class="verse-number">11</span> Wilt thou trust him, because his strength is great? or wilt thou leave thy labour to him? <span class="verse-number">12</span> Wilt thou believe him, that he will bring home thy seed, and gather it into thy barn? <span class="verse-number">13</span> Gavest thou the goodly wings unto the peacocks? or wings and feathers unto the ostrich? <span class="verse-number">14</span> Which leaveth her eggs in the earth, and warmeth them in dust, <span class="verse-number">15</span> And forgetteth that the foot may crush them, or that the wild beast may break them. <span class="verse-number">16</span> She is hardened against her young ones, as though they were not her's: her labour is in vain without fear; <span class="verse-number">17</span> Because God hath deprived her of wisdom, neither hath he imparted to her understanding. <span class="verse-number">18</span> What time she lifteth up herself on high, she scorneth the horse and his rider. <span class="verse-number">19</span> Hast thou given the horse strength? hast thou clothed his neck with thunder? <span class="verse-number">20</span> Canst thou make him afraid as a grasshopper? the glory of his nostrils is terrible. <span class="verse-number">21</span> He paweth in the valley, and rejoiceth in his strength: he goeth on to meet the armed men. <span class="verse-number">22</span> He mocketh at fear, and is not affrighted; neither turneth he back from the sword. <span class="verse-number">23</span> The quiver rattleth against him, the glittering spear and the shield. <span class="verse-number">24</span> He swalloweth the ground with fierceness and rage: neither believeth he that it is the sound of the trumpet. <span class="verse-number">25</span> He saith among the trumpets, Ha, ha; and he smelleth the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting. <span class="verse-number">26</span> Doth the hawk fly by thy wisdom, and stretch her wings toward the south? <span class="verse-number">27</span> Doth the eagle mount up at thy command, and make her nest on high? <span class="verse-number">28</span> She dwelleth and abideth on the rock, upon the crag of the rock, and the strong place. <span class="verse-number">29</span> From thence she seeketh the prey, and her eyes behold afar off. <span class="verse-number">30</span> Her young ones also suck up blood: and where the slain are, there is she.</p>
</div>
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
\begin{scripture}[Job][39]
\lettrine[lines=4]{K}{nowest} thou the time when the wild goats of the rock bring forth? or canst thou mark when the hinds do calve?
\vs{2}Canst thou number the months that they fulfil? or knowest thou the time when they bring forth?
\vs{3}They bow themselves, they bring forth their young ones, they cast out their sorrows.
\vs{4}Their young ones are in good liking, they grow up with corn; they go forth, and return not unto them.
\vs{5}Who hath sent out the wild ass free? or who hath loosed the bands of the wild ass?
\vs{6}Whose house I have made the wilderness, and the barren land his dwellings.
\vs{7}He scorneth the multitude of the city, neither regardeth he the crying of the driver.
\vs{8}The range of the mountains is his pasture, and he searcheth after every green thing.
\vs{9}Will the unicorn be willing to serve thee, or abide by thy crib?
\vs{10}Canst thou bind the unicorn with his band in the furrow? or will he harrow the valleys after thee?
\vs{11}Wilt thou trust him, because his strength is great? or wilt thou leave thy labour to him?
\vs{12}Wilt thou believe him, that he will bring home thy seed, and gather it into thy barn?
\vs{13}Gavest thou the goodly wings unto the peacocks? or wings and feathers unto the ostrich?
\vs{14}Which leaveth her eggs in the earth, and warmeth them in dust,
\vs{15}And forgetteth that the foot may crush them, or that the wild beast may break them.
\vs{16}She is hardened against her young ones, as though they were not her's: her labour is in vain without fear;
\vs{17}Because God hath deprived her of wisdom, neither hath he imparted to her understanding.
\vs{18}What time she lifteth up herself on high, she scorneth the horse and his rider.
\vs{19}Hast thou given the horse strength? hast thou clothed his neck with thunder?
\vs{20}Canst thou make him afraid as a grasshopper? the glory of his nostrils is terrible.
\vs{21}He paweth in the valley, and rejoiceth in his strength: he goeth on to meet the armed men.
\vs{22}He mocketh at fear, and is not affrighted; neither turneth he back from the sword.
\vs{23}The quiver rattleth against him, the glittering spear and the shield.
\vs{24}He swalloweth the ground with fierceness and rage: neither believeth he that it is the sound of the trumpet.
\vs{25}He saith among the trumpets, Ha, ha; and he smelleth the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.
\vs{26}Doth the hawk fly by thy wisdom, and stretch her wings toward the south?
\vs{27}Doth the eagle mount up at thy command, and make her nest on high?
\vs{28}She dwelleth and abideth on the rock, upon the crag of the rock, and the strong place.
\vs{29}From thence she seeketh the prey, and her eyes behold afar off.
\vs{30}Her young ones also suck up blood: and where the slain are, there is she.
\end{scripture}

##### Chapter 40

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="40">
<p><span class="drop-cap">M</span>oreover the LORD answered Job, and said, <span class="verse-number">2</span> Shall he that contendeth with the Almighty instruct him? he that reproveth God, let him answer it. <span class="verse-number">3</span> Then Job answered the LORD, and said, <span class="verse-number">4</span> Behold, I am vile; what shall I answer thee? I will lay mine hand upon my mouth. <span class="verse-number">5</span> Once have I spoken; but I will not answer: yea, twice; but I will proceed no further. <span class="verse-number">6</span> Then answered the LORD unto Job out of the whirlwind, and said, <span class="verse-number">7</span> Gird up thy loins now like a man: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me. <span class="verse-number">8</span> Wilt thou also disannul my judgment? wilt thou condemn me, that thou mayest be righteous? <span class="verse-number">9</span> Hast thou an arm like God? or canst thou thunder with a voice like him? <span class="verse-number">10</span> Deck thyself now with majesty and excellency; and array thyself with glory and beauty. <span class="verse-number">11</span> Cast abroad the rage of thy wrath: and behold every one that is proud, and abase him. <span class="verse-number">12</span> Look on every one that is proud, and bring him low; and tread down the wicked in their place. <span class="verse-number">13</span> Hide them in the dust together; and bind their faces in secret. <span class="verse-number">14</span> Then will I also confess unto thee that thine own right hand can save thee. <span class="verse-number">15</span> Behold now behemoth, which I made with thee; he eateth grass as an ox. <span class="verse-number">16</span> Lo now, his strength is in his loins, and his force is in the navel of his belly. <span class="verse-number">17</span> He moveth his tail like a cedar: the sinews of his stones are wrapped together. <span class="verse-number">18</span> His bones are as strong pieces of brass; his bones are like bars of iron. <span class="verse-number">19</span> He is the chief of the ways of God: he that made him can make his sword to approach unto him. <span class="verse-number">20</span> Surely the mountains bring him forth food, where all the beasts of the field play. <span class="verse-number">21</span> He lieth under the shady trees, in the covert of the reed, and fens. <span class="verse-number">22</span> The shady trees cover him with their shadow; the willows of the brook compass him about. <span class="verse-number">23</span> Behold, he drinketh up a river, and hasteth not: he trusteth that he can draw up Jordan into his mouth. <span class="verse-number">24</span> He taketh it with his eyes: his nose pierceth through snares.</p>
</div>
:::

\lettrine[lines=4]{M}{oreover} the LORD answered Job, and said,
\vs{2}Shall he that contendeth with the Almighty instruct him? he that reproveth God, let him answer it.
\vs{3}Then Job answered the LORD, and said,
\vs{4}Behold, I am vile; what shall I answer thee? I will lay mine hand upon my mouth.
\vs{5}Once have I spoken; but I will not answer: yea, twice; but I will proceed no further.

\vs{7}Gird up thy loins now like a man: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.
\vs{8}Wilt thou also disannul my judgment? wilt thou condemn me, that thou mayest be righteous?

\vs{11}Cast abroad the rage of thy wrath: and behold every one that is proud, and abase him.

\vs{21}He lieth under the shady trees, in the covert of the reed, and fens.

##### Chapter 41

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="41">
<p><span class="drop-cap">C</span>anst thou draw out leviathan with an hook? or his tongue with a cord which thou lettest down? <span class="verse-number">2</span> Canst thou put an hook into his nose? or bore his jaw through with a thorn? <span class="verse-number">3</span> Will he make many supplications unto thee? will he speak soft words unto thee? <span class="verse-number">4</span> Will he make a covenant with thee? wilt thou take him for a servant for ever? <span class="verse-number">5</span> Wilt thou play with him as with a bird? or wilt thou bind him for thy maidens? <span class="verse-number">6</span> Shall the companions make a banquet of him? shall they part him among the merchants? <span class="verse-number">7</span> Canst thou fill his skin with barbed irons? or his head with fish spears? <span class="verse-number">8</span> Lay thine hand upon him, remember the battle, do no more. <span class="verse-number">9</span> Behold, the hope of him is in vain: shall not one be cast down even at the sight of him? <span class="verse-number">10</span> None is so fierce that dare stir him up: who then is able to stand before me? <span class="verse-number">11</span> Who hath prevented me, that I should repay him? whatsoever is under the whole heaven is mine. <span class="verse-number">12</span> I will not conceal his parts, nor his power, nor his comely proportion. <span class="verse-number">13</span> Who can discover the face of his garment? or who can come to him with his double bridle? <span class="verse-number">14</span> Who can open the doors of his face? his teeth are terrible round about. <span class="verse-number">15</span> His scales are his pride, shut up together as with a close seal. <span class="verse-number">16</span> One is so near to another, that no air can come between them. <span class="verse-number">17</span> They are joined one to another, they stick together, that they cannot be sundered. <span class="verse-number">18</span> By his neesings a light doth shine, and his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning. <span class="verse-number">19</span> Out of his mouth go burning lamps, and sparks of fire leap out. <span class="verse-number">20</span> Out of his nostrils goeth smoke, as out of a seething pot or caldron. <span class="verse-number">21</span> His breath kindleth coals, and a flame goeth out of his mouth. <span class="verse-number">22</span> In his neck remaineth strength, and sorrow is turned into joy before him. <span class="verse-number">23</span> The flakes of his flesh are joined together: they are firm in themselves; they cannot be moved. <span class="verse-number">24</span> His heart is as firm as a stone; yea, as hard as a piece of the nether millstone. <span class="verse-number">25</span> When he raiseth up himself, the mighty are afraid: by reason of breakings they purify themselves. <span class="verse-number">26</span> The sword of him that layeth at him cannot hold: the spear, the dart, nor the habergeon. <span class="verse-number">27</span> He esteemeth iron as straw, and brass as rotten wood. <span class="verse-number">28</span> The arrow cannot make him flee: slingstones are turned with him into stubble. <span class="verse-number">29</span> Darts are counted as stubble: he laugheth at the shaking of a spear. <span class="verse-number">30</span> Sharp stones are under him: he spreadeth sharp pointed things upon the mire. <span class="verse-number">31</span> He maketh the deep to boil like a pot: he maketh the sea like a pot of ointment. <span class="verse-number">32</span> He maketh a path to shine after him; one would think the deep to be hoary. <span class="verse-number">33</span> Upon earth there is not his like, who is made without fear. <span class="verse-number">34</span> He beholdeth all high things: he is a king over all the children of pride.</p>

\begin{scripture}[Job][41]
\lettrine[lines=4]{C}{anst} thou draw out leviathan with an hook? or his tongue with a cord which thou lettest down?
\vs{2}Canst thou put an hook into his nose? or bore his jaw through with a thorn?
\vs{3}Will he make many supplications unto thee? will he speak soft words unto thee?
\vs{4}Will he make a covenant with thee? wilt thou take him for a servant for ever?
\vs{5}Wilt thou play with him as with a bird? or wilt thou bind him for thy maidens?
\vs{6}Shall the companions make a banquet of him? shall they part him among the merchants?
\vs{7}Canst thou fill his skin with barbed irons? or his head with fish spears?
\vs{8}Lay thine hand upon him, remember the battle, do no more.
\vs{9}Behold, the hope of him is in vain: shall not one be cast down even at the sight of him?
\vs{10}None is so fierce that dare stir him up: who then is able to stand before me?
\vs{11}Who hath prevented me, that I should repay him? whatsoever is under the whole heaven is mine.
\vs{12}I will not conceal his parts, nor his power, nor his comely proportion.
\vs{13}Who can discover the face of his garment? or who can come to him with his double bridle?
\vs{14}Who can open the doors of his face? his teeth are terrible round about.
\vs{15}His scales are his pride, shut up together as with a close seal.
\vs{16}One is so near to another, that no air can come between them.
\vs{17}They are joined one to another, they stick together, that they cannot be sundered.
\vs{18}By his neesings a light doth shine, and his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.
\vs{19}Out of his mouth go burning lamps, and sparks of fire leap out.
\vs{20}Out of his nostrils goeth smoke, as out of a seething pot or caldron.
\vs{21}His breath kindleth coals, and a flame goeth out of his mouth.
\vs{22}In his neck remaineth strength, and sorrow is turned into joy before him.
\vs{23}The flakes of his flesh are joined together: they are firm in themselves; they cannot be moved.
\vs{24}His heart is as firm as a stone; yea, as hard as a piece of the nether millstone.
\vs{25}When he raiseth up himself, the mighty are afraid: by reason of breakings they purify themselves.
\vs{26}The sword of him that layeth at him cannot hold: the spear, the dart, nor the habergeon.
\vs{27}He esteemeth iron as straw, and brass as rotten wood.
\vs{28}The arrow cannot make him flee: slingstones are turned with him into stubble.
\vs{29}Darts are counted as stubble: he laugheth at the shaking of a spear.
\vs{30}Sharp stones are under him: he spreadeth sharp pointed things upon the mire.
\vs{31}He maketh the deep to boil like a pot: he maketh the sea like a pot of ointment.
\vs{32}He maketh a path to shine after him; one would think the deep to be hoary.
\vs{33}Upon earth there is not his like, who is made without fear.
\vs{34}He beholdeth all high things: he is a king over all the children of pride.
\end{scripture}

##### Chapter 42

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Job" data-chapter="42">
<p><span class="drop-cap">T</span>hen Job answered the LORD, and said, <span class="verse-number">2</span> I know that thou canst do every thing, and that no thought can be withholden from thee. <span class="verse-number">3</span> Who is he that hideth counsel without knowledge? therefore have I uttered that I understood not; things too wonderful for me, which I knew not. <span class="verse-number">4</span> Hear, I beseech thee, and I will speak: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me. <span class="verse-number">5</span> I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee. <span class="verse-number">6</span> Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes. <span class="verse-number">7</span> And it was so, that after the LORD had spoken these words unto Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends: for ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job hath. <span class="verse-number">8</span> Therefore take unto you now seven bullocks and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you: for him will I accept: lest I deal with you after your folly, in that ye have not spoken of me the thing which is right, like my servant Job. <span class="verse-number">9</span> So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went, and did according as the LORD commanded them: the LORD also accepted Job. <span class="verse-number">10</span> And the LORD turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before. <span class="verse-number">11</span> Then came there unto him all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all they that had been of his acquaintance before, and did eat bread with him in his house: and they bemoaned him, and comforted him over all the evil that the LORD had brought upon him: every man also gave him a piece of money, and every one an earring of gold. <span class="verse-number">12</span> So the LORD blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning: for he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses. <span class="verse-number">13</span> He had also seven sons and three daughters. <span class="verse-number">14</span> And he called the name of the first, Jemima; and the name of the second, Kezia; and the name of the third, Kerenhappuch. <span class="verse-number">15</span> And in all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job: and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren. <span class="verse-number">16</span> After this lived Job an hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons' sons, even four generations. <span class="verse-number">17</span> So Job died, being old and full of days.</p>
</div>
:::

\begin{scripture}[Job][42]
\lettrine[lines=4]{T}{hen} Job answered the LORD, and said,
\vs{2}I know that thou canst do every thing, and that no thought can be withholden from thee.
\vs{3}Who is he that hideth counsel without knowledge? therefore have I uttered that I understood not; things too wonderful for me, which I knew not.
\vs{4}Hear, I beseech thee, and I will speak: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.
\vs{5}I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee.
\vs{6}Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.
\vs{7}And it was so, that after the LORD had spoken these words unto Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends: for ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job hath.
\vs{8}Therefore take unto you now seven bullocks and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you: for him will I accept: lest I deal with you after your folly, in that ye have not spoken of me the thing which is right, like my servant Job.
\vs{9}So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went, and did according as the LORD commanded them: the LORD also accepted Job.
\vs{10}And the LORD turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.
\vs{11}Then came there unto him all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all they that had been of his acquaintance before, and did eat bread with him in his house: and they bemoaned him, and comforted him over all the evil that the LORD had brought upon him: every man also gave him a piece of money, and every one an earring of gold.
\vs{12}So the LORD blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning: for he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses.
\vs{13}He had also seven sons and three daughters.
\vs{14}And he called the name of the first, Jemima; and the name of the second, Kezia; and the name of the third, Kerenhappuch.
\vs{15}And in all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job: and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren.
\vs{16}After this lived Job an hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons' sons, even four generations.
\vs{17}So Job died, being old and full of days.
\end{scripture}
